author: Bill Haufe

Burnham has new title, old approach

 July 18, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports

 CAMBRIDGE — Rob Burnham's title has changed, not his approach."I'm competitive to a fault maybe," Burnham said. "I will lose sleep to prepare for a game. I will stress and wake up at three in the morning and go draw stuff on the board; paper, pad at the computer. Watch film and do all those things.
"But I did all those things before I was a head coach," Burnham continued. "So that's not new for me. The only thing that's new for me is there's a fancy title in front of my name."
That title is head football coach at Cambridge-South Dorchester High.
"Super excited," said Burnham, who was announced as the Vikings' new head coach earlier this month. "It's been a long time coming. Excited for the opportunity to be head coach for sure.
"I just like working with kids," the 45-year-old Burnham added. "I like taking a kid and giving him an opportunity to make himself better through athletics."
Though he was a head wrestling coach for two years at William Fleming High in Roanoke, Virginia, this is Burnham's first head coaching job in football.
He succeeds Toby Peer, who coached Cambridge-SD the past three seasons, compiling an 18-14 record, which included reaching last year's Class 1A state semifinals, where the Vikings lost to eventual state champion Fort Hill.
Burnham said Peer has retired from education and is now working for Altec Industries selling trucks.
"I didn't think he'd step away early. But that's what he decided to do," Burnham said of Peer.
Burnham, who has coached high school football for 25 seasons, began working with Peer at William Fleming. When Peer accepted the head coaching job at South Hagerstown he brought Burnham with him as offensive line coach and offensive coordinator. Together they helped the Rebels go 57-25 during Peer's eight years as head coach, and watched running back Isiaha Smith set the state single-season rushing record with 2,918 yards in 2013.
Peer stepped away as head coach at South Hagerstown when he became the school's athletic director. But he returned to the coaching ranks in 2021, when he took over at Cambridge-SD. Again, he brought his offensive line coach and OC with him.
A native of Kalamazoo, Michigan who played left tackle in high school before heading off to Western Michigan University, Burnham will continue handling the offensive and defensive lines despite his new title. He said he isn't sure if he will be offensive coordinator, but knows for certain he wants to run the football.
"We want guys to get out and attack downfield and run the football effectively at every turn," Burnham said. "As an offensive line guy, if I can run the ball every single play and win I'm good with that. Nobody wants to come and watch that, but I'm over it already. If we win the game we win the game. I throw it three times and we win, I'm good with it. I throw it 50 times and we lose I'm not good with it."
Burnham taught eighth grade math for two years at Mace's Lane in Cambridge before accepting a special education position at Cambridge-SD last year.
"Most of the kids in this building I know," Burnham said. "I either had them in class or they knew who I was from being over at Mace's Lane."
The Vikings lost only five players from last year's 9-3 team, including starting quarterback Blake LaBelle, now at Frostburg State University. The fact that the bulk of last year's Class 1A East championship team is back should help, especially on the defensive side, where Burnham plans to change little.
"Defensively, we're probably going to be almost identical because I think our kids played well to the 3-4 scheme with the two high safeties," Burnham said. "Our kids run fast enough to keep everything in front of us. And it's not a bend-but-don't-break philosophy, but it's more of a we're going to give you a little bit and then take away what you try to get, if that makes sense. We run well enough at every position defensively that we're going to be OK."
Cambridge-SD lost four coaches from last year's staff, but Burnham thinks he can handle that transition as well.
"I feel confident in my ability to assemble a staff that can put kids in a place to be successful in most situations," Burnham said. "There's a virtual guarantee that I'll encounter a situation that I haven't encountered before. But I have a number of people that I can call and talk to and get sound advice, people to bounce ideas off of if there's a situation I don't like."
At the top of Burnham's don't-like list is losing.
"I'm a bad loser. My wife said it's not one of my great qualities," Burnham said. "But I'm going to do things very, very similar to the way I've always done before."

TALL TASK

 WORTON — Harold Somerville's biggest challenge heading into his third year as Kent County High's head football coach may not be figuring out who he's going to plug in at left tackle or outside linebacker.No, Somerville's biggest task may be simply getting his players to believe in themselves.
"The talent's there," Somerville said after Saturday morning's scrimmage against North East of Cecil County. "They got to believe it."
Somerville isn't saying the Trojans are going to compete for titles or make a deep playoff run. But in Saturday's scrimmage against North East there were plenty of encouraging signs.
Terrell Fennell slipped around left end, found an open sideline and blazed about 40 yards for a touchdown. There were a handful of other big-chunk plays, and the defense showed solid pursuit to the ball and gang tackled.
Somerville can also drop back to late last season in terms of his team's growth. One week after getting routed by Snow Hill 47-6 in their regular-season finale, the Trojans upended the Eagles, 34-18, in the first round of the Class 1A East Region playoffs.
"We're not looking bad," Somerville said. "I was pleased with Saturday. We know we've got some work to do, but I was pleased with it."
The offensive line lost two starters from last year's 2-9 squad, and that's where the most work may be needed in terms of getting stronger.
Sophomore Taeshaun Demby (6-foot-1, 250 pounds) starts at center, and is flanked by senior right guard Harrison Gibby (6-0, 190) and sophomore left guard Andrew Fennell (5-9, 200). Senior Wyatt Toulson (5-10, 180) starts at left tackle, while senior Wesley Townsend (6-4, 315) is at right tackle.
"I think we can compete with the other 1A schools," Somerville said of Bayside rivals Cambridge-South Dorchester, Colonel Richardson, Snow Hill and Washington. "I honestly feel as though if our line just gives the quarterback enough time to get the ball off I think that we can really compete. And I feel real comfortable with our receivers and our running backs."
He should considering most every one of them returns from last year.
Sophomore Dwan Harris (6-1, 170) is back at quarterback and looks to have a solid cast of backs that include senior Terrell Fennell (5-7, 150), juniors Scottie Ford (5-9, 140) and Tyrel Dean (5-8, 165), and sophomore Kalief Roberts (5-9, 150).
The receiving corps also looks strong, led by senior Jonah Somerville (5-7, 152) — the coach's son — who can line up in the slot or wide, as well as at quarterback or in the backfield. Harris' other two wide targets are sophomore Dylan Hurtt (5-8, 130) and Ramon Peterson (5-9, 150), while seniors Jysir Valentine (6-4, 240) and Shakur Wilson (6-1, 180) are at tight end.
Defensively, Kent will go with either a 4-3 or 5-3 scheme, with Andrew Fennell and Townsend at the tackles, and Toulson at nose, depending on the lineup. Valentine and Wilson will be the ends.
Coach Somerville admitted his linebacking unit struggled some against North East, but part of that was because Ford and Dean did not play. When it has a full complement of players, Kent will have junior Zayvion Brown (5-9, 160) and Ford as outside backers and Dean inside.
The secondary appears to be a strongpoint, with Terrell Fennell and Peterson at the corners, and Somerville and Roberts playing safety.
"I think our defense, at least in the second half, we were playing better than the offense," said Coach Somerville, who played nose tackle on Kent County's 1989 and '90 Class 1A state championship teams. "Especially our DBs. Our DBs are very experienced. They know how to read the ball."
Jonah Somerville will handled kickoffs and Harris will punt.
"I honestly believe, if they really believe in themselves and the jell together, that we can go to that next level and not just win two games like we have been the last couple years," Coach Somerville said.

title: BANKING ON EXPERIENCE
author: Bill Haufe
content:
BANKING ON EXPERIENCE

 August 28, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports

 AMERICAN CORNER — James Jackson isn't used to this.Seemingly everywhere Colonel Richardson High's head football coach looks this preseason there's a senior here and a senior there.
"I need to talk to (longtime assistant and former head coach) Neil Lambert, but I believe this is the biggest senior class Colonel football's ever had," Jackson said. "Under my supervision it's definitely the most."
And for that reason optimism is high for a group that would like to notch seven or eight regular-season victories and possibly match, or even exceed, the postseason run of the 2021 team that made a bunch of school history, which included reaching the Class 1A state quarterfinals for the first time.
"They're all talking about making a deep playoff run," Jackson said. "They're just looking forward to getting back to where we were their freshman year."
The Colonels look to have the talent and certainly the experience to make a push in that direction after going 4-6 a year ago, which included a 4-0 mark against Bayside 1A competition.
Seniors dominate both sides on the ball, with 6-foot-2, 195-pound quarterback Tarron Hammond directing the Double Wing T attack for a third straight year. Behind him are senior wingbacks Dylan Cecil (5-6, 140) and Eamare Jones (5-8, 155), senior fullback Collin Brewer (5-10, 200) and junior wingback Derrick Mitchell (5-11, 185), who led the Colonels in rushing a year ago. Junior wingback Bradley Thomas (5-9, 205) and senior fullback Chatydrick Pickrom (5-11, 230) could also be rotated into the backfield.
Senior tight ends Domnique Caven (6-0, 175) and Carter Turbitt (5-11, 180) provide two nice targets for Hammond, as well as additional push for the Colonels' steady-as-it-goes run game.
"I think clock control is always in our favor," Jackson said. "So running the football, trying to keep the ball in our possession as long as possible, wearing defenses down, that's what we're known for. If we can continue that, we have more success when we have the ball longer than our opponent."
Though Jackson has yet to settle on a starting right tackle, the remainder of the line is all seniors. Gavin Weiss (5-9, 230) is at center, with Chris Rockwell (5-10, 225) at right guard and Duilio Berduo-Morales (5-8, 235) at left guard. Stevens Austinville (6-3, 200) starts at left tackle.
"The seniors have been together for three years," Jackson said. "It's just now making it all come together."
What may help pull things together this season was what Jackson thought was missing in 2023 — senior leadership.
"We only had two seniors last year," Jackson said. "So this senior class now, none of them knew how to become a leader. I feel like now there's more talking in practice. There's quite a few of them trying to be leaders. So if we can get all the guys to follow behind these guys we should be pretty good."
The defense also has the potential to be pretty good.
Rockwell and Brewer, who shared the team lead in sacks last year with 10, line up at the ends, with Berduo-Morales at one tackle and Pickrom (8½ sacks), who can be a big-time difference maker, at the other tackle. If that group can tie up opposing linemen, inside linebackers Thomas and Cecil, and outside backers Mitchell, Jones and junior Carlens Jean Baptiste (5-6, 140) should be in position to make tackles.
Caven and Turbitt are back at the corners, while junior Jayquan Wilkins (5-7, 145) and sophomore JaZir Dickerson (6-0, 170) are the safeties.
"Coverages have got to get better, but in a week or two I think we'll be closer to where we need to be," Jackson said. "But we looked a lot better on our tackling in the scrimmage (against Sussex Tech) than we did all last season. Last season there was a lot of miss-tackles early. But in the scrimmage I thought with did a good job of gang tackling. And the first man to the ball was actually either holding on waiting for help, or making the tackle.
Since its history-making playoff run of 2021, Colonel — after taking a first-round forfeit over Washington in the 2022 playoffs — has been knocked out of the postseason by Bohemia Manor the last two years, including last year's 12-7 first-round loss.
"This group of starters haven't been past the first round of the playoffs," Jackson said. "They're looking for a deep playoff run this year. I feel coming in with experience, that hopefully will carry us to a good season."

ON THE REBOUND

 September 3, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports

 EASTON — If.That's how Matt Griffith started his preseason commentary entering his 10th year as Easton High's head football coach.
Griffith's first word is certainly understandable considering starting quarterback Mikey O'Connor suffered a season-ending injury in Week 2 of last year, which played a huge role in the Warriors going 1-8.
"If we can healthy, 'cause we got low numbers, and continue to improve we should be able to put a good product out on the field," said Griffith, who also lost his starting quarterback, Mason Ledford, in Week 2 of the 2017 season.
A 6-foot-3, 195-pound senior, the left-handed throwing O'Connor returns as the starter behind center, and is backed by 6-3, 220-pound sophomore Brady Walls, a transfer from St. Mary's.
"Mikey looks really good," said Griffith, of the third O'Connor brother to start at quarterback for the Warriors. "The transfer kid (Walls) is pretty good, too."
Easton's backfield not only looks pretty good, but appears plenty deep. Junior Dustin Blue (5-11, 212) and sophomore Jordan Horsey form a nice, physical one-two punch. Freshman Jamier Copper (5-9, 195), juniors JaSere Molina (5-7, 160) and Tayshaun Roberts (5-8, 180), and senior Najhay Smith (5-9, 175) are also expected to get rotated into the ground game.
"Really deep at running back," Griffith said. "We've got five kids that I think we can hand the ball off to and we're not missing much of anything. The first two are bruisers with Dustin and Jordan. They're a load to tackle. And JaSere gives us a nice change of pace with a different type speed. He's pretty quick."
Quickness is also found in a receiving corps that welcomes the return of senior standout Chase Raab (5-11, 180), who never got on the field a year ago after an injury in 7-on-7 summer play wiped out his entire season.
"That's a big, big lift for us, getting him back," Griffith said of Raab. "And he's 100 percent, which is good."
The rest of the receiving cast doesn't look too shabby either, with junior wideouts Carter Mooney (5-11, 180) and Logan Friend (5-10, 160), and seniors Jaden Prestwood (6-3, 215) and Finn Gunshenan (5-10, 170). The Warriors' biggest threats though may be at slot. Senior Colin Mooney (5-7, 170) returns and is joined by juniors Diontaye Copper (5-10, 185), Kyree Acree (5-11, 175) and Zach Barnhart (5-8, 180).
"We have a good core that we can cycle through and get breaks on offense, and not have any drop-offs because some of these guys are going to be playing on the defensive side of the ball as well," Griffith said. "It's going to be nice to be able to go, 'Kyree you're going in for Diontaye, and Zach,' and vice versa to be able to get them some breaks."
Easton lost four starters from the offensive line, with junior right tackle Tymiere Thomas (5-10, 240) the lone returner. But Griffith has liked his young group's development and praised the work of assistants Drew Griffith — his son — and Dave Perillo, the longtime line coach at Queen Anne's County.
Junior Trushun Truxon Jr. (5-11, 190) starts at center, with freshman guard Brady Gilliece (6-3, 225) and sophomore tackle Xavier Stowers (6-3, 230) lining up on his left, and junior guard Jack Chapple (6-4, 220) joining Thomas on the right side. Senior Nathaniel Lapp (6-7, 225) and juniors Paul Whitlock (5-10, 210) and Tracey Gore (6-0, 285) could also be moved in and out of the lineup.
"Young. Inexperienced. But a very good work in progress," Griffith said of his offensive front. "They're improving every day. It's good sized and most of those kids spent time in the weight room."
The defense has many of the same faces, with a few different ones sprinkled through.
Sophomore Elias Leonard (5-10, 305) is at nose guard, where Groce and Truxon could also get time. Thomas is back at one tackle and has looked great in the preseason, according to his head coach. Teaming with him up front will be a rotation of Stowers, Lapp, Gilliece, Whitlock and Chapple.
Inside linebacker should be a strength, with Blue and Horsey starting, and Copper, Gunshenan and junior Alex Rhodes (5-10, 180) in reserve. Prestwood and Roberts start outside, but Griffith noted sophomores Nevin Whitaker (5-9, 190) and Teddy Antal (6-0, 175) could see time.
The secondary is athletic and fast, with Acree, Copper, Friend, Molina and Carter Mooney at the corners. Raab starts at free safety, while Colin Mooney and Barnhart are at strong safety.
"They're learning the new system under coach (Al) Waters," Griffith said of his new defensive coordinator, who has coached at Queen Anne's and Cambridge-South Dorchester. "They're enjoying it. It's not a lot different from what we're used to. We're starting to do less thinking and play a little faster."
Senior Dominic Stanco, who also plays soccer, handles the place-kicking chores. Horsey and Walls will punt.
"Very excited to see how they continue to improve," Griffith said of his team.
Easton opens Friday when its hosts North East of Cecil County, coached by Warrior alum Taylor Slaughenhoupt. Kickoff is scheduled for 7 p.m.

 CAMBRIDGE — He's been running offenses for 20 years, including the last four seasons at Cambridge-South Dorchester High.But Rob Burnham, who took over as Vikings head coach in July, knows a thing or two about defense.
"For the last 13 years I've just been an offensive guy," said Burnham, who during that span was an assistant to former Vikings head coach Toby Peer, first at South Hagerstown, then at Cambridge-SD. "But I've coached defense previously for a dozen years so it's not new. Just having to oversee everything is a little bit different. But I like doing it."
Burnham has liked what he's seen on both sides of the ball this preseason from a team that returns 18 starters from last year's 9-3 Class 1A East Region championship outfit that reached the state semifinals, where it lost to eventual state champ Fort Hill.
The graduation of Class 1A first-team all-state quarterback Blake LaBelle — now at Frostburg State University — may affect the passing game, but Burnham thinks 6-foot-2, 190-pound senior Anthony Hughes can run the offense just fine.
"We lose the all-state quarterback and that stings a little bit," Burnham said. "But we can find other ways to make up for the great things he did for us, and do the best that we can with the kids that we have and find a way to make them successful.
"We don't have an all-state quarterback this year I don't believe, unless he just cranks it up and starts throwing it a whole lot better," Burnham said of Hughes, who is backed up by freshman Nate Twilley (5-11, 200). "But Anthony's strength is not his arm, it's his legs. He has the ability to throw, but he's a better runner than he is a thrower."
The Vikings could again have one of the Bayside Conference's better running attacks, led by returning starter Sterling Perkins, a 5-8, 180-pound junior, who along with Hughes helped the Vikings reach the Class 1A state basketball championship game back in March. Senior Will Jackson (5-10, 170) and juniors Ra'Qwan Cornish (5-11, 150) and Jayden Hollowel (5-10, 175) all have the potential to bust the big play every time they touch the ball.
"I think our run game is certainly going to drive the bus," Burnham said.
Covering Cambridge-SD's fleet of receivers could drive opposing defensive coordinators crazy. Heading that cast is senior Antonio Blueford (6-4, 190), a four-year starter, and junior Magestic Jones (5-11, 180) a three-year returning starter. They are joined by juniors Tamyron Evans (5-10, 160), TJ Wilson (6-2, 175) and Leonbre Chester (6-1, 180), and senior Kimir Lake (6-0, 160).
"We've got some kids that run fast and jump high," Burnham said. "The plan is to try to find the best things that we can execute and get the ball in our playmakers' hands in space and let them do their thing. We try to maximize their ability."
Senior left guard Omarian Travers (6-4, 255) is the lone returning starter on the offensive line. He starts between freshman center Telorian Williams Jr. (6-4, 265) and sophomore left tackle K'Marion Hall (6-2, 240). The right side of the line has sophomore Jeffrey Sellman (5-11, 240) at guard and junior Russell Johnson (6-2, 200) at tackle. Senior KaMarii Stanley (6-2, 190), who's been on varsity all four years, is at tight end.
"I think we've done well up front blocking," Burnham said. "We've had a tremendous amount of improvement that we've done over the course of the last year or so in offensive line play. Our group of kids that we have are picking up things pretty quickly, and I think we did well with our run game."
Cambridge-SD has done a solid job against the run in preseason, with sophomore JaKuez Sneed (5-9, 210) starting at nose guard flanked by senior tackles Jairyn Lewis (6-2, 195) and Stanley.
The tall, rangy Blueford has the potential to be a wrecking machine at outside linebacker, a unit that includes Hughes, Wilson and Chester. Senior Christen Dockins (5-11, 175), who led the team in tackles a year ago, returns at inside linebacker, teaming with senior Donnell Cephas (5-10, 190), Perkins and Hollowell.
"Defense will be the backbone of our team," Burnham said. "We're pretty stout against the run and we're fast everywhere. I don't want to sound conceited, but we don't have slow kids on defense. Every position is fast."
That's especially true in the secondary where Lake will start at corner with either Jones or Cornish, while Jackson and Evans start as safeties.
"I've been pretty impressed by our ability to tackle," Burnham said. "We've only missed a handful of open-field tackles in our scrimmages but we've had a couple of mishaps in coverage. But it's to be expected when you go out and scrimmage. You try to teach from that stuff. It's a learning experience, and you get better and you don't make that mistake again. If we get good film and we teach from it the scrimmage is successful."
Junior Collin Bair handles the kicking duties.
"I can't wait to get on the field Friday night and see what our kids can do," said Burnham of the Vikings' season opener at North Caroline. "And I think our kids are excited too. That's ultimately the important part."

A FINE BLEND

 CENTREVILLE — Brian Mooney likes the blend Queen Anne's County High's football team has going this preseason.The Lions' second-year head coach likes how his offensive spread game is mixing with the return of former head coach Donny Graef's double-wing approach.
Mooney likes that his offense returns rock-solid 1,000-plus yard rusher John Connolly and sophomore sensation Ja'Dereon Thompson. He likes how his almost new offensive line is coming together under Graef's tutelage.
Mooney also likes his defensive blend, where he and Graef have been molding ends Amari Baynard and Conlan Nagle, where the electric Thompson and two-time all-Bayside Conference corner Carter Dickey are again roaming the secondary, and where Parker Whiteford — after a year at DeMatha — has returned in an alpha role at inside linebacker.
"It's a work in progress," said Mooney, who went 6-5 a year ago. "We're transitioning."
Perhaps the biggest transition is on offense, where Graef, the school's winningest head coach — compiling a 176-95 record over 25 years — returns as an assistant. Among Graef's duties will be coaching the offensive line, which was the longtime domain of another Lions' coaching great, Dave Perillo, now at Easton.
"We have a brand new line," said Mooney, noting senior Nate Mayoral did get a couple spot starts last season. "He's the only one with varsity starting experience. All those guys are cutting their teeth under coach Graef which is awesome.
Centering that line will be 5-foot-11, 225-pound junior Drew Sutton. Juniors Brian Maleski (5-10, 185) and Mac Windsor (6-foot, 210) line up at guard, though senior Ethan Wheaton (5-10, 195) figures to be worked in. Junior Elijah Goldsborough (6-4, 280) is at right tackle and Mayoral (6-3, 260) is on the left side.
"To learn from a Hall of Famer is an awesome opportunity for those guys," Mooney said of his offensive front which includes senior tight ends Christian St. Germain (5-11, 190) and Whiteford (6-1, 215). "They're really soaking it in. Coach Graef, he has high expectations, and when they don't meet those expectations he holds them to it. It's really cool to watch that blend with the skills we have."
The Lions' skill group looks strong. Junior Lance Arnold (5-10, 180), who started the last six games a year ago, returns at quarterback, with sophomore Carter Hercher (6-0, 190) at backup.
A first-time all-conference pick a year ago, Connolly (6-0, 210), a senior, returns to lead a backfield that includes juniors Dorrin Phillips (5-9, 195) and Dickey (5-8, 155), and sophomore Hunter Kelly (5-9, 170).
"We have some skill guys that are going to make any offensive line look good," Mooney said. "John Connolly, we expect to lean on him very heavily."
But as far as play calling goes, Mooney plans to balance his spread philosophy with Graef's old-school style.
"We're kind of working on doing some things Coach Graef is more familiar with," Mooney said. "Bringing him in as offensive line coach makes sense to go back to doing a lot of the things we were successful doing before. It's been a good blend."
Adding to that blend is a receiving corps that includes juniors Baynard (6-4, 190) and Brooks Blodgett (6-0, 175), and senior Nagle (6-2, 190). But the biggest threat is Thompson.
"Ja'Dereon obviously is a human highlight reel," Mooney said.
Thompson is also a threat to blaze into the end zone every time he handles a kick. Last year as a freshman he averaged 41 yards on kickoff returns, taking three in for touchdowns, and 25 yards on punt returns, which included one touchdown.
"He's a blessing to have," Mooney said of Thompson. "And the way he practice and carries himself. I mean some of the stuff you see. ... I always tell the college coaches I talk to, if you could see his practice tape you'd offer him right now."
The Lions look to have more experience on defense, where Thompson returns at deep safety in a secondary that features Dickey and Kelly at strong safety, Blodgett and junior Wyatt Wilhoit (5-8, 155) at corner, and Hercher, who can be inserted at corner or safety.
Wheaton returns at starting tackle and is joined by Sutton, who had spot starts last year, and Goldsborough, who can give either a break when needed. Bookending that trio are ends Baynard and Nagle.
The biggest boost to the defense though figures to be the return of Whiteford at inside linebacker, where he plays along side senior Frank Constantino (5-9, 210) and Maleski.

author: Bill Haufe
content:
PUTTING IT TOGETHER

 Ja'Mion Franklin has graduated from Duke University.Kendron Wayman is one game deep into his senior season at Wake Forest. And Nasai Bell is on West Virginia University's roster at safety.
Zymear Smith appears to be the next football standout from North Caroline High headed for the Division I ranks, having verbally committed to the University of Maryland.
And while the talented 6-foot, 175-pound senior halfback figures to draw plenty of attention this season from opponents, Smith knows he's just one part of the Bulldogs' offense and its all-senior backfield.
"He's a solid team player for us," North Caroline second-year head coach Nic McMorris said of Smith, who was the team's third leading rusher a year ago on the way to earning first-team all-Bayside Conference honors. "He wants everybody to kind of lift their game, himself included. He doesn't think he's above the program or anything like that. He's taking a lot of pride this season, especially in his blocking. He's a solid leader for us."
He's also part of what again should be one of the Bayside Conference's more solid backfields with the return of fellow seniors Tyson Weber and Justice Hall.
"Tyson is a very hard-nosed runner," McMorris said of the 5-10, 180-pound halfback. "And honestly, he has the ability to be our top receiver. It's saying a lot, but he runs a very good route, and he's got 10½-inch hands. His agility is through the roof, and he's a hard enough runner who prides himself in running between the tackles."
Then there's the 6-foot, 205-pound Hall, who can fill the role of battering ram quite nicely.
"Justice is a very hard-nosed runner that I'm looking to lean on a lot," McMorris said. "There's not a lot that's flashy, but he kind of prides himself on being a throwback football player. Exactly how the fullback should be."
Add to that mix Bell's successor at quarterback, senior Corey Bunce (6-foot, 170), who also hopes to show his running abilities when given the opportunity.
"We're putting it together," said McMorris, who will have junior Owen Walstrum (5-11, 165) backing up Bunce, and senior Tannor Wood (5-9 140) and junior Darrian Somerville (5-7, 140) coming in to give the starters a breather when needed. "I'm real happy with our run game. And it's not just my starting guys. I know Tannor and Darrian can get it done with the run game and the pass game."
The pass game includes a four-man rotation at wide receiver — seniors Jackson Conn (5-8, 145), Shelton Nichols (6-0, 160) and Derek Jones (6-1, 160), and junior Glother Gabriel (5-10, 180) — as well as junior tight end Declan Egan (6-2, 205).
There is experience on the offensive line, with the return of junior center Grayson Martin (6-1, 250), senior left tackle Owen Piavis (6-1, 210), and senior Cam King (6-4, 240), who moves from tight end to starting right tackle. Joining that group are sophomore left guard Demarcus Forsyth (6-5, 320) and junior right guard David Kusyk (5-10, 195). McMorris said junior Wyatt Eaton (6-2, 210), one of the team's best offensive linemen, figures to work his way into that starting group as he returns from injury.
"We still need to clean some things up just in terms of kids' specific jobs," McMorris said of his offense. "I think some kids are worrying about other kids' jobs. It's affecting the play because they're so worried about another block. It's just a matter of everybody jelling together and having faith in each other to get the job done. Once we get that we should have a really solid running game."
The defense also looks solid.
McMorris plans to go with a four-man rotation at the tackles, with Martin and King starting, and sophomore Xavier Comacho (5-10, 255) and freshman Desmeir Duckery (6-0, 210) stepping in when needed. Piavis, a first-team all-conference pick, returns at defensive end along with Egan and junior Caden Deavers (5-10, 205). All-Bayside linebacker Tommy Morris graduated, but the Bulldogs looked to be in good shape, with Gabriel and Somerville starting inside, and senior David Aviles (6-0, 195) and Hall staring on the outside.
Smith and Weber figure to form one of the conference's more formidable cornerback combinations. Wood starts at safety, with Walstrum also seeing time in the secondary.
"I think we're still putting it together," McMorris said of his defense. "We have a lot of guys that are kind of playing in new positions. We're getting there."
McMorris knows there may be pressure after going 9-2 in his first season as head coach, but that pressure may not necessarily translate into a repeat of, or improving on last season.
"It's more knowing that we have a good team and we should do well; more of just living up to the expectations that we've laid out for ourselves," said McMorris, who will have Mason Shilling handling the kicking duties.
"We often tell them, it's a thing we've said for years, 'You're never as good as you think you are. You're never as bad as you think you are,'" McMorris added. "And it comes down to, you don't read into the outside hype of what's going on. Like our film is going to tell us how we played and we need to be our number one critics of ourselves. Anybody else's opinion is rat poison."

title: New-look Buccameers begin Davis era
author: Bill Haufe

New-look Buccameers begin Davis era

 The head coach is new, and so are many of the faces in starting roles on both sides of the ball.But not everything has changed with Kent Island High's football program, which is set to begin the Zach Davis era Friday when the Bucs host Parkside at Andy Schipul Stadium at 6 p.m.
"We kept a lot of things very similar to how things have been done. I think that's helped," said Davis, who begins his 10th season as a head coach, but his first in Stevensville as the successor to Bryon Sofinowski, who retired after last year. "Even though there's a whole bunch of new guys, it's not like it's brand new to the coaches and players. It's pretty similar."
One thing that has remained the same is senior quarterback Gavan Henry, who returns after helping the Buccaneers to a 9-3 season a year ago, which included upending North Caroline in the second round of the Class 2A East Region playoffs.
"He's throwing the ball really well," Davis said of Henry, who will be backed up by junior Ryan Brestensky. "Good arm, good command of the offense. He's a good player for us."
Though last year's starting backfield graduated, starters Nate Green (senior wingback) and Jaxson Hess (junior single back) did get playing time in reserve roles last season. Junior wingbacks Connor Byrne and Kerry O'Brien figure to also get plenty of touches.
"We're going to come downhill at you," Davis said. "We're going to run zone, power schemes, counter schemes, some buck-sweep schemes. Our passing game comes off our run game. And then we have a spread package, where we can throw it some."
When Henry does throw, his targets will include senior Richie Guthrie and juniors Luke Umstot and Isaiah Diaz at wideout, and senior tight end Jackson Towers.
The Bucs graduated their entire offensive line from last year, so Davis, who coaches the offensive line, has been busy rebuilding. Senior James Prince starts at center between junior guards Mike Luttrell and Gerson Chevez. Senior Joe Guida is at right tackle, while Jeremiah Bounds starts on the right side.
"They're a really good group and they're working hard," Davis said of the offensive front. "But I'm their position coach so I'm partial. I think they're coachable, and I think if someone's coachable they can play pretty quickly, as long as they have the physical tools."
Perhaps the biggest returner for the Bucs is longtime defensive coordinator Tim Goodrich, who watched his unit notch three shutouts last season, and limit two other opponents to just seven points.
"He tells me all the time if I can score 14 points we'll win a lot of games," Davis said of Goodrich, who looks to replace three all-Bayside Conference first-team selections in lineman Brady O'Neal, defensive back Tucker Claxton, and linebacker Giuseppe Mellinger, the conference defensive player of the year.
Junior Greg Coffey, Bounds and Guida start up front, with senior Keegan Green and Towers at ends. Junior Roy Scott and O'Brien are at inside linebacker, with Green and Hess manning the outside backer spots. The secondary includes a combination between junior Taray Wright, Andy Bennett, Umstot, and Byrne.
Spencer Chappell kicks for the Bucs and Keegan Green punts.
"I think you feel excitement before every game," said Davis when asked about heading into his 10th season opener, the first nine of which were as a head coach in West Virginia. "That's good though. That means it means something. It's coming quickly. Then we'll move on to the next one."

 EASTON — Mikey O'Connor may have been the happiest player on the field. And Chase Raab wasn't too far behind.O'Connor, who suffered a season-ending injury in last year's second game, ran for a pair of touchdowns and threw for two more Friday night, as Easton High's football team opened its season with a dominating 43-0 victory over North East of Cecil County.
"He's a great athlete," North East head coach Taylor Slaughenhoupt said of O'Connor, Easton's senior quarterback. "And we knew it coming in. Fantastic athlete and he did what he does. There's a reason why … he's missed pretty much two years and he still has college offers. That kid can play flat out. Just like his brothers (former Easton quarterbacks Ryan and Kevin)."
The Warriors scored on their first possession, junior running back Dustin Blue's 8-yard touchdown run capping an eight-play, 66-yard scoring drive with 8 minutes, 21 seconds left in the first quarter. Dominic Stanco drilled the first of his five point-after kicks to make it 7-0.
North East senior quarterback Garrette Kirby ran for 13 yards and a first down on the first play of the Indians' next possession. But North East went nowhere with a fresh set of downs, as Easton's Tymiere Thomas sacked Kirby on third down, forcing a punt.
One play later, O'Connor found space around right end and raced 34 yards for a touchdown. Stanco's second PAT made it 14-0 with 5:06 left in the first quarter.
"Feels great to be back out here playing again, and to get a good win like this," said O'Connor, who carried four times for 84 yards. "Definitely feels great."
Easton extended its lead to 22-0 on its next possession, as O'Connor (7 of 14, 121 yards, one interception) hit Raab in stride for a 52-yard scoring play, then found Diontaye Copper for the two-point conversion. A senior wide receiver, Raab missed all of last year because of an injury suffered during summer 7-on-7 play.
"Mikey did a good job," Easton head coach Matt Griffith said. "He managed the offense and took what the defense gave him all night long. He made some big plays with his arm and his legs tonight. And that's what we expect out of him."
Easton looked ready to take a 22-0 lead into the break. But a snap from center sailed over the head of North East punter Craig Aubrey, giving the Warriors the ball on the Indians' 5-yard line. On the next play, O'Connor raced virtually untouched around right end for a 5-yard touchdown that helped Easton to a 29-0 halftime cushion.
"They had a ton of great plays tonight," O'Connor said of his young offensive line. "And they really showed how good they can be. A lot of our touchdowns and big plays, give credit to them for that, especially on my runs."
The Warrior set the running clock in motion with 10:09 left in the third quarter as O'Connor rolled left and hit Copper for a 35-yard scoring strike. Stanco's kick made it 36-0.
Easton padded its lead with 4:30 remaining when backup quarterback Brady Walls connected with Colin Mooney for a 52-yard touchdown play.
"It was a good night," Griffith said. "We still have a lot of things to clean up on. I thought we did enough things well to put a good product on the field tonight."
Easton, which notched its first shutout since Week 2 of the 2021 season, held North East to just 39 yards rushing on 22 carries, dropping the Indians for losses seven times. Kirby, who was harassed seemingly from start to finish, completed 5 of 18 passes for 65 yards and was intercepted by Zach Barnhart.
"He was running for his life," Slaughenhoupt said of his quarterback. "We weren't protecting him. I mean we couldn't stop a leak up front.
"I thought we'd be able to run the ball on them," continued Slaughenhoupt, who graduated from Easton. "I thought it would be a competitive game and it kills me. We just did a lot of things tonight that were not us. We had a really good week (of practice) and a really good (preseason) camp, and it just wasn't there tonight."

North East wide receiver Deyshawn Henderson had two receptions for 41 yards. ... O'Connor was intercepted in the second quarter by Nathan Tesch, who caught a ball that deflected off Warrior receiver Carter Mooney.

title: Vikings rush past Knights

 CAMBRIDGE — Rob Burnham is among the football coaching crowd who stresses the importance of the second half's first possession.The last possession of the first half proved pretty important as well for Burnham's Cambridge-South Dorchester High team Friday night.
Sterling Perkins hauled in a 14-yard touchdown pass just before the end of the first half, then scored on a 3-yard run to open the second half, to help give the Vikings separation on the way to a 49-21 victory over Century.
"I tell our kids all the time when we get in the locker room that the first possession of the second half is the biggest possession of the game," said Cambridge-SD's first-year head coach after his team improved to 2-0. "And I believe that. You open the game and score, that's OK because there's a lot of ballgame left. But when you open the second half (and score). ... And I thought it was big that we scored right before halftime and then we got the possession again. So that gives us the two-score lead. That's huge. Huge."
After a scoreless first quarter, Cambridge-SD senior quarterback Anthony Hughes scored on runs of 20 and 55 yards to help stake the Vikings to a 14-0 lead with 9 minutes, 18 seconds left in the second quarter. Collin Bair drilled both point-after kicks.
The Knights (0-2) rallied though. Jonathan Ferguson scored on a 1-yard run up the middle, but the point-after boot sailed wide left, leaving Century trailing 14-6.
Cambridge-SD drove from its 40 to the Knights' 20, where Dylan Vroom intercepted Vikings backup quarterback Nathan Twilley and raced 80 yards up the sideline for a touchdown. Ferguson's two-point conversion run tied the game at 14-all with 3:02 left before halftime.
The Vikings came right back, as Hughes lofted a pass toward the end zone that Perkins made a nice over-the-shoulder grab on for a 14-yard touchdown and a 20-14 lead with 7.6 remaining in the first half. Cambridge-SD bobbled the snap from center on the extra-point attempt, and settled for a six-point lead entering the break.
The Vikings needed just three plays to expand that lead on the first possession of the second half. Perkins ran for gains of 17 and 27 yards before he took a handoff and made a quick juke into the end zone for a 3-yard touchdown. Hughes hit Antonio Blueford with a two-point conversion pass for a 28-14 lead just 42 seconds into the third.
On its next possession, Century tried to convert a fourth-and-four from its own 31. But quarterback Jacob Dexter fired incomplete, turning the ball over to the Vikings. On the next play, William Jackson swept right and blazed into the end zone for a 31-yard touchdown. Bair added the PAT for a 35-14 lead with 9:08 to go in the third.
Century pulled within 35-21 with 4:50 left in the third, as Ferguson bulled his way into the end zone from 2 yards out, then booted the point-after.
The Knights though could not stop Cambridge-SD's big plays.
On its ensuing possession, Hughes broke free for his third touchdown run, this one covering 42 yards for a 41-21 cushion with 3:34 left in the third.
Cambridge-SD again stopped the Knights on fourth down, but penalties from the Vikings back to their own 6-yard line. It didn't matter, as Perkins took a handoff, found a seam up the middle, and bolted 94 yards for a touchdown. Blueford made a diving grab on Hughes' two-point pass for a 49-21 lead.
"We're going to get better," Burnham said. "The things we struggled with today we'll make improvements on. We have to be better than we were tonight that's for sure."

title: Warriors survive Bulldogs' rally
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Warriors survive Bulldogs' rally

 September 20, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports

 EASTON — It didn't matter that North Caroline High's football team had lost its first two games this season.The Bulldogs just scared Easton head coach Matt Griffith. And in a furious fourth-quarter span of just over four minutes they showed why, shaving a 28-point Warrior lead to just seven.
That's when Mikey O'Connor took over. Easton's senior quarterback ran for a pair of first downs and threw for another in the final 2:52 Friday night to finally secure a 28-21 victory that pushed the Warriors' record to 3-0.
"They got great athletes all over the field," Griffith said of North Caroline. "They've struggled early on, but you saw exactly how explosive they can be, and how quick they can be explosive. That's what I was worried about. Sometimes you can do all the right things, but sometimes really good athletes can make plays. And that's a lot of what happened in the last five minutes of the twilight zone that we're calling it."
O'Connor hit Diontaye Copper for a 35-yard touchdown pass 1:41 into the third quarter, and Dominic Stanco tacked on the point-after kick for a 28-0 Easton lead.
The Warriors had not allowed a point all season until North Caroline's Tyson Weber scored on a 16-yard run with just under seven minutes left in the game, drawing the Bulldogs (0-3) within 28-7. Mason Shilling added the extra point.
Easton went three-and-out on its next possession, with O'Connor booting a quick kick to North Caroline's 27. Bulldog senior quarterback Corey Bunce hit Derek Jones for 13 yards, then connected with Zymear Smith for a 33-yard pickup. Weber scored on a 27-yard touchdown run on the next play and Shilling again converted the PAT, narrowing Easton's lead to 28-14 with 3:57 left.
North Caroline recovered the ensuing onsides kick at the Warrior 47. Bunce hit Jones for a 20-yard gain. Easton's Tymiere Thomas sacked Bunce for a 5-yard loss. But the Bulldogs' quarterback fired toward the end zone on the next play, and watched the ball deflect into the hands of Jones for a 33-yard touchdown. Shilling's point-after kick made it 28-21 with 2:52 remaining.
"Hell of a comeback," North Caroline head coach Nic McMorris said. "I'm so proud of the resilience of our guys. It was the first time that we recognized this team.
"They're a great team," McMorris added of Easton. "They have such a dynamic offense. But we were moving the ball and just kept shooting ourselves in the foot. And then we just started playing inspired football."
North Caroline drove from its 38 to the Easton 12 when it fumbled the ball away late in the first quarter. But the Bulldogs regained possession four plays later when O'Connor's pass was deflected and intercepted by Smith. Again Caroline moved the ball, marching 32 yards to the Warrior 8. But the Bulldogs again fumbled, with Easton recovering at the 1.
Easton's next drive ended with a fumble, giving North Caroline possession at the Warrior 25. But North Caroline went no where on three plays. Shilling came on to attempt a 40-yard field goal, but slipped on his approach, the kick falling well short.
The Warriors, who took a 7-0 lead on O'Connor's 3-yard touchdown run and Stanco's PAT with 3:54 left in the first quarter, stretched their lead to 14-0 with 2:11 left in the first half, when Jordan Horsey slammed in from five yards out. Stanco again made the extra point.
Easton took advantage of a short Caroline punt, as O'Connor hit Carter Mooney for 18 yards, and Copper for 17 yards before scoring on a 2-yard run for a 21-0 halftime lead.
"We came out with a game plan and we executed very well," Griffith said. "I think we did a lot of really good things early, even with two turnovers. Those are our first two turnovers of the year. We were able to bounce back."
So was North Caroline.
"No excuses," Griffith said. "Caroline's a good football team. They're a very good football team for being 0-3."
It's one-time 28-point cushion reduced to just seven, Dustin Blue recovered the onsides kick for Easton after North Caroline had gotten within 28-21.
O'Connor ran for three yards before Caroline called time. O'Connor then ran for eight yards and a first down. North Caroline stuffed Easton's quarterback for no gain on the next play and again burned a timeout. O'Connor then fired an 11-yard dart to Carter Mooney for a first down, then found room around left end for a 22-yard pickup and a first down that clinched the win. O'Connor took a knee on the next two plays to bleed the final minute.
'We got up and then we just kind of let off," O'Connor said. "And we just can't do that against a great team like this. Great first half. Then the second half we slipped off. But we need to play two halves of football."
Griffith agreed but applauded his quarterback.
"He did a phenomenal job," Griffith said of O'Connor. "And he took control at the end of the game to make sure we were able to seal the victory."

That lead stood until late in the third quarter, when Kent Island's Jaxon Hess raced 25 yards around right end for an apparent touchdown. But that score was erased when the Buccaneers (3-1) were called for holding. Four plays later, Kent Island punted the ball to the Easton 1.
The Warriors pieced together a 10-play, 99-yard drive that ended with O'Connor hitting Chase Raab for a 24-yard touchdown. Dominic Stanco's point-after boot made it 28-10 with 8:49 remaining in the game.
"That was huge," said Griffith of Kent Island having a score taken away before the Warriors lengthened their advantage to 18. "We talked about trying to finish. And I think that's the biggest thing. We've focused all week long on execution and finishing the game. And I thought tonight we did."
Kent Island came right back, as Henry hit Jackson Towers for a 64-yard touchdown pass that — together with Spencer Chappell's PAT — pulled the Bucs within 28-17 with 6 minutes left.

Coming out in the third quarter and stopping them. Then we stalled and it was a defensive game most of the (scoreless) third quarter. Then we got back on track offensively and that's was good to see."
Easton drove 87 yards on its first possession to take a 7-0 lead on O'Connor's 5-yard touchdown run around left end.
The Warriors forced a Bucs' three-and-out, and had moved back into Kent Island territory, when Hess intercepted O'Connor in the left flat and sprinted 55 yards for a touchdown. Chappell's PAT forged a 7-7 tie with 5:40 left in the first quarter.
The game remained close. O'Connor scored on a 1-yard run, but Stanco's extra-point attempt was blocked, giving the Warriors a 13-7 lead with under 3 minutes left in the first quarter.
Kent Island shaved that lead to 13-10 just 53 seconds into the second quarter, when Chappell hammered a 38-yard field goal.

"Good football team," Davis said of Easton. "Definitely a physical football team. We weren't as physical as we needed to be tonight. And we had some big plays taken away by penalties."
Henry fired his second touchdown pass with 43.2 seconds left in the game when he hit Isaiah Diaz for a 29-yard score.
"We've got work to do obviously," Davis said.
O'Connor said the same thing of Easton.
"I thought this win was big for us. Kind of a like statement," said O'Connor, who leads Easton into another battle of unbeatens next Friday at defending Class 2A state champion Stephen Decatur. "I feel like I played all right. But I could have done a lot of things better."

 Queen Anne's County High isn't the fastest or strongest football team in the Bayside Conference.But four games into the season, the Lions are playing with a longtime program staple — grit.
"They're gritty," head coach Brian Mooney said after Queen Anne's — playing its first home game of the season — evened its record last Friday night with a 20-15 victory over James M. Bennett. "There's no quit on this team. We're not going to quit at any point. Adversity struck and they smiled back and we ended up pulling it out."
Adversity has been stalking the Lions since the beginning of the season.
Starting right tackle Elijah Goldsborough went down during a Week 1 loss at Stephen Decatur. Starting quarterback Lance Arnold suffered a season-ending injury on the final drive of a Week 2 setback at Chesapeake-Anne Arundel.
Despite those two injuries, Queen Anne's notched its first win of the season Sept. 19 with a 24-0 shutout of Wicomico.
But the Lions lost two more starting pieces on offense. Starting left tackle and team captain Nathan Mayoral got injured last week in practice. Then Drew Sutton, who starts at center and defensive tackle, got injured during Friday's win over the Clippers.
"We're shuffling some guys around for sure," Mooney said.
Junior Gannon Brown, who was getting limited playing time, has taken over for Goldsborough at right tackle. Levi Frank has stepped into Mayoral's spot on the left side. And Ethan Wheaton is at center.
"We're getting back to playing Queen Anne's football," Mooney said. "We're going to line up and punch you in the teeth. It's a next-man-up philosophy and hats off to (assistant) coach (Donny) Graef doing his job on the offensive line. We've had four different starting combinations on our line now in the last four weeks. We're just trying to get some consistency there."
Then there is sophomore quarterback Carter Hercher, who on Friday carried nine times for 58 yards that included a 3-yard touchdown run and a QB sneak for the two-point conversion.
"He was a DB (defensive back) at the beginning of the season and we flipped him into the quarterback role," Mooney said of Hercher.
The Lions got a huge performance from running back John Connolly, who carried 27 times for 147 yards, including touchdowns runs of 18 and 8 yards. Hunter Kelly had 56 yards rushing on six touches, and Parker Whiteford logged eight tackles.
UNBEATEN VIKINGSCambridge-South Dorchester on Friday pushed its record to 4-0 for the first time since 2014 with a 23-0 shutout of Colonel Richardson.
"To be fully honest I didn't expect us to shut 'em out," Vikings first-year head coach Rob Burnham said. "I hoped to slow them down. I was very pleased with our defensive performance. I know the weather played a role in that, but our kids responded to the challenge that was laid before them, and I'm very pleased with the result."
The second half was played in a heavy rain, but Cambridge-SD had already built a big enough lead at that point.
Sterling Perkins racked up 175 yards rushing on 14 carries that included first-quarter 73-yard touchdown romp. The Vikings fattened their lead in the second quarter, as senior quarterback Anthony Hughes hit Antonio Blueford with a 44-yard touchdown pass. Hughes later scooped a fumble and returned it for a touchdown, then ran in the two-point conversion on a bobbled snap from center. Taybrion Watts had a safety for the Vikings' other points.
"Our kids are playing really hard," Burnham said of his team's 4-0 start. "They bought into what I asked them to do. They're very coachable. They're doing the little things right for the most part, and they recognize where we have deficiencies and we've made improvements. We've tried to get better each and every time we touch the field."

 It took until the middle of the third quarter Thursday night for Cambridge-South Dorchester High's football team to get going.It's taken the Vikings a great deal longer though to reach the midway point of a season with a 5-0 record.
Down by a point with 9 minutes, 22 seconds remaining in the third quarter, Cambridge-SD closed with a flourish, scoring the game's last 39 points en route to a 46-8 victory over Kent County in Worton, giving the Vikings a 5-0 record for the first time since 2000.
"I guess our kids fell asleep on the bus and didn't wake up," Cambridge-SD head coach Rob Burnham said of his team's slow start. "We tried to get there early enough to get them ready to go. It took us being down by a point before they decided, 'Oh, maybe we should go and actually play.' And that was really frustrating for me."
Cambridge-SD led 7-0 and was driving early in the third quarter, when Kent County's Jonah Somerville intercepted Viking quarterback Anthony Hughes' pass and returned it for a touchdown. Tyrell Fennell ran in the two-point conversion, nudging the Trojans (1-4) to an 8-7 lead.
That seemed to only arouse the Vikings, who got their running game cranked up and took control.
"It took awhile," Burnham said of his offense finding its groove. "I'm not sure why, but they figured it out, and then we were able to move the ball, both passing and running. And it didn't really matter who was doing it."
Cambridge-SD amassed 379 yards rushing on 35 carries. Leading the way was Hughes, who carried 10 times for a game-high 152 yards, including touchdowns runs of 34 and 20 yards. Running back Sterling Perkins Jr. had touchdown runs of 16, 2 and 25 yards as part of his 13-carry, 132-yard effort.
William Jackson added a 36-yard touchdown run, and finished with 75 yards on eight carries. And freshman backup quarterback Nate Twilley had a 13-yard touchdown run.
"The strength of our team right now is running the football," Burnham said. "So we want to make sure that we can establish the strength of our team and continue to move forward, and do the things that we do."
Hughes was 4 of 9 passing for 32 yards, and Twilley completed both his attempts for 33 yards.
The 2000 Vikings went 10-0 during the regular season under then head coach David Bromwell before losing to Southern Garrett in the Class 1A quarterfinals.

title: Colonel ends skid in a rush
author: Bill Haufe

 AMERICAN CORNER — James Jackson did a lot of preaching in practice this week.A whole lot of preaching.
"We've been preaching all week, the backs hitting the holes," Colonel Richardson High's head football coach said. "They've been running past the holes, or cutting out too early. So tonight they actually hit the holes and stayed in the holes, and they found green. They found a lot of green."
Ja'Zir Dickerson returned the opening kickoff 75 yards for a touchdown and Derrick Mitchell ran for three touchdowns Friday night, as the Colonels celebrated homecoming with a 56-0 shellacking of Lancaster, Virginia.
"Coach James preached to me at practice, 'You stay in the wedge on the kick return,'" Dickerson said. "He was like, 'It's going to open up.' We watched film, seen they didn't tackle very well. So they kicked it to me and I just knew I had to get in the wedge and take one home and bring the energy."
Dickerson grabbed the opening kickoff, moved upfield, then broke left and down the home sideline to give Colonel (2-3) a 6-0 lead with only 13 seconds off the clock. Morgan Demir drilled the first of his four point-after kicks.
"That's big," Jackson said of Dickerson's game-opening score. "Anytime you come out and you score right off the jump then you make a team a little nervous. Then you don't know what's coming at you.
"We set that up all week," Jackson continued. "I was watching their special teams on film and I told our guys that 'They don't stay in their lanes, and if we set it up, we can return the opening kickoff.' And we did. That definitely set the tone for the rest of the night. That brought the energy."
Colonel, which snapped a three-game losing streak, scored on all six of its first-half possessions in addition to Dickerson's opening romp.
Mitchell, who carried five times for 113 yards, scored his first touchdown from 3 yards out with 6:17 left in the first quarter. Quarterback Tarron Hammond ran in the two-point conversion for a 15-0 lead.
Hammond squeezed into the end zone on the Colonels' next possession and watched Demir convert his second PAT for a 22-0 lead after one quarter.
"They had to bring back the intensity they had in Week 1," Jackson said in reference to Colonel's 55-0 win over Washington. "And I needed the team that played Kent Island (a 38-33 loss) to play the same way tonight, but come out with a win. I think they listened. They answered the call."
Dickerson, who also finished with 113 yards rushing on just three carries, and who had a first-quarter punt return for a touchdown erased by a penalty, was sprung for a 64-yard touchdown run with 9:46 left in the second quarter. Collin Brewer bulled in for the two-point conversion and a 30-0 lead.
Colonel scored three more touchdowns in a little over 5 minutes to close the first half. Hammond hit Carter Turbitt with a 30-yard touchdown pass, Mitchell scored on a 31-yard burst around right end, and Chatydrick Pickrom seemingly moved the bulk of Lancaster's defense during an 11-yard touchdown run up the middle that gave Colonel a 50-0 halftime lead.
Mitchell scored the only touchdown of the second half when he broke loose for a 37-yard touchdown jaunt in the third quarter.
"We came out with a lot more energy and we played as a team," Mitchell said. "We blocked for each other. We did everything we were supposed to do. Great blocking."
Jackson agreed.
"They did a tremendous job tonight," Jackson said of his offensive line. "I've been looking for the o line all year. Tonight we were running as one unit. It wasn't one side here and one side there. It was everybody working for us tonight with our o line."
Colonel stopped Lancaster (2-4) six times of fourth down and forced two punts. Lancaster's other possession ended with the first-half clock running down.

author: Bill Haufe
content:
Next-man-up approach still working for QA's

 It was just another weekend for Queen Anne's County High's football team.It was another game tainted by injury. Wait, make that injuries.
And yet despite losing two defensive starters and their starting quarterback, the Lions again found a way to log another victory last Friday, stretching their win streak to three with a convincing 43-6 rout of North Caroline.
"Hats off to our defensive coordinator, coach Jude Mandes," Queen Anne's head coach Brian Mooney said after the Lions registered their most lopsided victory of the season while holding North Caroline to a season-low six points. "He does a great job of mixing up his coverages and the looks that he gives defenses. He's been really dialed in with his blitz packages as of late. He's continuing to grow just like our defense."
Also continuing to grow is the Lions' injury list.
On the first play of the game Friday, starting defensive end Conlan Nagle got rolled up on, suffering a leg injury. Amari Baynard stepped in for Nagle.
All-Bayside Conference starting safety Carter Dickey injured his arm during the second defensive series. Sophomore Alex McDonald went in for Dickey and got his first playing time of the year, and "played really well," Mooney said.
The defense got another outstanding effort from inside linebacker Parker Whiteford (10 tackles).
"They moved the ball on us pretty good that first drive, but he's just an alpha," Mooney said of Whiteford. "He's just a man-child. I don't know what else to say about the kid. It's an awesome treat to have. Him and coach Jude have a great unison and between the two of them, he's kind of like another Jude out on the field."
Mooney also praised the play of junior cornerback Wyatt Wilhoit, who finished with six tackles, including a sack, and a forced fumble.
"Kind of getting his first varsity experience, he had a great night," Mooney said of Wilhoit. "Had a forced fumble inside the 20 on one of their first drives, and then I think he had the game-changing play. Right before halftime they were driving (to Queen Anne's 30) and he came off the edge on one of coach's blitzes and just cracked the quarterback for about a 10-yard loss. It just kind of changed the whole momentum of the game I felt."
Queen Anne's then lost starting quarterback Carter Hercher, who got hurt while attempting a pass in the third quarter.
Before getting injured, Hercher had completed 6 of 7 passes for 104 yards, and carried three times for 11 yards.
The Lions didn't stall though, moving sophomore Ja'Dereon Thompson behind center in the wildcat formation. Thompson finished the game with touchdown runs of 25 and 40 yards as part of a six-carry, 92-yard rushing effort, and caught two passes for 62 yards.
"We call it the flashback with Ja'Dereon, and we've been practicing that just in case something like that happened," Mooney said. "And he went in and we didn't miss a beat."
Senior running back John Connolly also didn't miss a beat, as he carried 16 times for 190 yards, with touchdown runs of 1, 10 and 11 yards.
"We've been really working on his technique, some of his footwork stuff in the week leading up, and he just hit it on a tee," Mooney said of Connolly. "He was cutting really well behind the guards on power and finding that groove. He was averaging 11 yards a carry. We're going to ride our guy."
Queen Anne's hosts Kent County (1-4) for homecoming on Saturday at noon.
NO PANICDespite Friday's 38-0 loss at defending Class 2A state champion Stephen Decatur, Easton head coach Matt Griffith doesn't see his team unraveling.
"Obviously it was not what we expected," Griffith said after the Warriors slipped to 4-1. "We expected to give them a game at least. We did early."
The Seahawks (5-0) were up 7-0, scored early in the second quarter, then erupted for three more touchdowns in the final 5:02 before halftime.
"There was a tipped ball that goes off a receiver's hands, and we had some debacles up front driving," Griffith said. "Again, good football team. They've got some great athletes. We just didn't execute our part. If we want a chance to redeem ourselves we have to play really good and redeem ourselves against them maybe in the postseason."
Easton was held to 12 rushing yards on 11 attempts, and senior quarterback Mikey O'Connor completed 7 of 20 passes or a season-low 27 yards.
"We didn't respond in a big game, big atmosphere," Griffith said. "And while Decatur's a very good football team we did not play our best football. And this game does not dictate the season. You get to dictate the rest of the season and that starts (last) Saturday morning.
Easton hosts Parkside (2-3) on Friday at 6:30 p.m.
BUCS STOPPEDThe surprise from last weekend may have been Wicomico's 21-14 upset of Kent Island on Saturday in Stevensville. Bucs quarterback Gavan Henry completed 10 of 25 passes for 122 yards and a touchdown to Jackson Towers, and running back Jaxson Hess finished with 12 carries for 44 yards and a touchdown.

 Nic McMorris was fired Monday morning as North Caroline High's head football coach midway through his second season.The Bulldogs went 9-2 and reached the second round of the Class 2A East Region playoffs last year in McMorris' first season as head coach. The team was expected to have another strong season this year, with running backs Zymear Smith and Tyson Weber, and all-Bayside Conference defensive end Owen Piavis returning.
But the Bulldogs have struggled, falling to 0-5 after last Friday night's 43-6 loss at Queen Anne's, their most lopsided loss of the season.
McMorris said he received a phone call Monday morning from North Caroline principal Matt Spiker, who wanted to schedule a face-to-face meeting with the head coach.
"I will say he tried to have me in the office. He tried to have a face-to-face conversation," McMorris said Wednesday morning during a phone interview. "I wanted to have a conversation right then and there, so we talked on the phone. I was in St. Michaels, and I was like, 'I don't want to be thinking about this for an hour and a half.'"
McMorris said Spiker told him he was being let go as head football coach. McMorris did not say why he was let go.
Reached by phone Wednesday morning, Spiker declined to comment, referring the matter to Caroline County Public Schools public information officer Sandi Barry.
"Mr. McMorris is no longer employed by CCPS (Caroline County Public Schools), however we wish him success in future endeavors," Barry said, reading from a statement. "As with all personnel matters, we cannot provide any further information."
McMorris, 34, who is not a teacher, was North Caroline's junior varsity head coach before being named offensive coordinator for the varsity for the 2022 season. When then-head coach James McCormick stepped down after 22 seasons, McMorris was named the school's head varsity coach.
"I'm obviously disheartened and pretty upset about it," McMorris said of the decision. "But I want the kids to go out and win on (Thursday) despite me not being there."
McMorris said junior varsity head coach Heath Wilkins has been promoted to varsity head coach and will be on the sideline Thursday when North Caroline travels to play at James M. Bennett in Salisbury.
"I am genuinely happy for Heath Wilkins, who's taking over," McMorris said. "He's a fantastic coach and literally my number two. He supported me the whole time."
McMorris finishes with a 9-7 career record at North Caroline.
Wilkins, 49, who's been with North Caroline's program for more than five years, was in his third season as junior varsity head coach before his promotion. He played football at Howard High School and then played semi-pro ball for 10 years.
"It's bittersweet," Wilkins said of being named McMorris' successor. "I consider Nic a friend. It's just a bad situation, but I am excited.
"It's a high profile position, and who wouldn't be nervous," Wilkins said of beginning his first varsity head coach job.

Bennett rallied from a 15-point halftime deficit to defeat visiting North Caroline, 27-21, spoiling the head coaching debut of North Caroline's Heath Wilkins.
"There was a really good feeling out there for that first half," said Wilkins, who was named head coach after North Caroline fired Nic McMorris this past Monday. "We felt good going into the game. We knew we'd be able to compete."
The Bulldogs (0-6) weren't only competing, but leading the Clippers, 21-6, at halftime — matching the most points they had scored in an entire game all season when they lost at Easton, 28-21, in Week 3.

"We have a package of plays where we just try to get him the ball anyway we can," Bennett head coach Greg Lasinski said of Smullen. "Heckuva player. I think he's the most under recruited player in the Bayside (Conference) right now. Whatever we ask him to do he can do it. He's explosive. He's just one of those kids you're lucky to have on your team because he can flip the game in your favor in a hurry."

Parkside's Nazere Sturgis intercepted Easton quarterback Mikey O'Connor (13 of 27, 211 yards, two touchdowns, three interceptions) less than 2 minutes into the second quarter. Parkside recovered an Easton fumble on the first play of the second half, setting up Bratten's 1-yard touchdown run. Harmon ran in the two-point conversion for a 29-15 lead with just under 10 minutes remaining in the third quarter.

 CENTREVILLE — Ja'Dereon Thompson knows a little about Queen Anne's County High's football history."When I was in eighth grade, KJ Smothers scored five touchdowns against Parkside one homecoming," Thompson said of the former Lions rushing standout.
After rushing for three touchdowns and passing for a fourth — all in the first half — Thompson was lobbying to get back on the field during homecoming Saturday afternoon at Lions Stadium. But with three regular-season games and at least one playoff contest still on the docket, Queen Anne's head coach Brian Mooney opted to keep his electric sophomore on the sideline.
"We told him 'We just want to get out of here healthy,'" Mooney said. "We haven't had a game yet where we've had no injuries. This was the first one that we got out of with no injuries."
The Lions not only got away injury free Saturday, but notched their second shutout of the season while extending their winning streak to four via a 45-0 victory over Kent County before a large homecoming crowd.
"He's special," Mooney said of Thompson, who started his first game at quarterback after the Lions lost starter Lance Arnold to injury in Week 2 and backup Carter Hercher to injury last week. "Four touchdowns in the first half. He wanted more, but I told him, 'Look man, we got to save you for the next game as we keep going."
Mooney's reasoning was understandable, considering the Lions (4-2) prior to Saturday had lost two quarterbacks, both starting offensive tackles, their starting center — who also started at defensive tackle — a defensive end and a cornerback all to injury.
Queen Anne's second-year head coach had most of his starters on the sideline during the second half after the Lions got off to their best start of the season, taking a 38-0 lead into the locker room.
"We talked about kind of starting fast, Mooney said. "It was something we haven't done all year. Most of the time we're like a second-half team. This time we came out in the first half and executed, and that first drive was a real long drive; took about seven or eight minutes off the clock. We pounded it down, got a touchdown out of it."
After receiving the opening kickoff, Queen Anne's ran 14 running plays covering 73 yards and eating close to 8 minutes of clock before senior John Connolly (9 carries, game-high 76 yards rushing) scored on a 2-yard run. Thompson ran in the two-point conversion for an 8-0 lead with 3:38 left in the first quarter.
Connolly gave the ball back to Queen Anne's, when he intercepted Kent quarterback Dwan Harris on the Trojans' first drive. Thompson (9 carries, 70 yards) dashed 16 yards around right end for a touchdown and Levi Frank added the point-after for a 15-0 lead with 13.2 seconds left in the first quarter.
Queen Anne's next points were set up by punter Ethan Keppler, who booted a 55-yard punt to the Trojans' 1-yard line. Two plays later, Kent's Jysir Valentine was stacked up and dropped for a safety and a 17-0 lead.
Thompson showed why he's nicknamed "Flash" on the ensuing kick, darting through traffic before getting knocked out of bounds at the Kent 16. The Trojans (1-5) looked like they might avoid a deeper deficit, but on a fourth-and-nine, Thompson, weaved his way to a 15-yard touchdown before Frank again hammered the PAT through for a 24-0 lead with 4:47 remaining in the first half.
"I think we're playing amazing," Thompson said. "With me at quarterback, it's like Lamar Jackson, and Derrick Henry with John Connolly. And then you've got the blockers. They're stepping up to play. It feels great right now. We're rolling right now."
Queen Anne's continued rolling, scoring on its next two possessions. Chance Hegedus wrestled a ball away from a defender for an 18-yard pass reception from Thompson with 3:07 left in the first half. Thompson added his third rushing touchdown with 26.4 seconds to go in the half, racing untouched around left end for a 10-yard score before another Frank PAT gave the Lions a 38-0 halftime cushion.
Parker Whiteford's 7-yard touchdown run and Frank's fifth extra-point kick pushed Queen Anne's to a 45-0 with 1:15 remaining on a running third-quarter clock.
Whiteford had a greater impact at inside linebacker, though, leading a defense that held Kent County to 49 yards rushing and 13 yards passing. Queen Anne's stopped seven of the Trojans' eight third-down attempts, forced three punts and one quick kick, had two interceptions, recovered a fumble, and foiled Kent's one fourth-down attempt.
"Defensively, I think we've been locked in all year long," Whiteford said of a unit that since giving up 35 points in a season-opening loss to defending Class 2A state champion Stephen Decatur — the Seahawks' lowest point total of the season so far — has yielded an average of just 7.4 points a game and notched two shutouts. "We're going out there doing our jobs. Coach Jude (Mandes) puts us in a good spot to keep growing and be good."
Whiteford attended DeMatha last year, where he played early in the season but saw limited duty after the starting linebacker he replaced returned.
"I'm real happy to be back," said Whiteford, who finished with nine tackles, three for losses against the Trojans. "This is the most fun I've had ever playing football. I love playing in front of my home crowd. It's amazing."

Warriors rally three times before edging Lions
