 It may not have matched the significance of the 2014 playoff between the two schools, but on an emotional level it came close.Mikey O'Connor hit Chase Raab with a 10-yard touchdown pass with 1 minute, 21 seconds remaining, and Zach Barnhart made his second interception with 53 seconds left Thursday night, as Easton High's football team rallied for a 27-26 victory over Queen Anne's County at Lions Stadium in Centreville.
The victory strengthened Easton's No. 2 seeding in the approaching Class 2A East Region playoffs behind undefeated and defending 2A state champion Stephen Decatur.
"For coach (Al) Waters and the rest of the guys that joined the staff it meant a lot for us to get a win there," Easton head coach Matt Griffith said Friday of Waters, his defensive coordinator who was a one-time head coach at Queen Anne's.
"But more importantly with that, we had a little bump in the road; two-game losing streak," Griffith continued. "And a young group of kids who are still trying to figure out to be mature on the football field and learn how to win. And they learned how to win last night. We could have folded the tent a few times."
Winners of four straight, Queen Anne's (4-3) jumped to a 14-0 first-quarter lead. DeRodney Smith (15 carries, 101 yards) scored on a 21-yard touchdown run, but Easton's Logan Friend blocked the extra point. Ja'Dereon Thompson then intercepted O'Connor and made an 84-yard touchdown return. Harris ran in the two-point conversion for a two-touchdown lead.
Easton (5-2) trimmed its deficit to 14-7, when O'Connor (12 of 20, 178 yards, three touchdowns, interception) connected with Colin Mooney for a 27-yard touchdown pass with 4:27 left in the first quarter. Dominic Stanco tacked on the extra point.
O'Connor's 1-yard touchdown run around left end and Stanco's second point-after kick pulled the Warriors even at 14-14 just 55 seconds into the second quarter.
But Queen Anne's responded, as John Connolly (12 carries, 101 yards) scored on an 8-yard run with 3:25 left in the first half for a 20-14 lead. Easton's Nathan Lapp blocked the extra point.
Barnhart intercepted Lions quarterback Carter Hercher with 30 seconds left in the first half, setting up O'Connor's touchdown pass to Diontaye Copper with 10 seconds to go before halftime. Stanco's PAT gave Easton a 21-20 lead.
The Warriors took the opening kickoff and drove 77 yards to the Queen Anne's 1, where they fumbled, the ball recovered by the Lions' Amari Baynard.
Queen Anne's put together a 97-yard drive that ended with Connolly's 3-yard touchdown run for a 26-21 lead. The Lions' two-point bid was stopped.
Easton regained the lead at 27-26, when O'Connor hit Raab with a 10-yard touchdown pass in the left side of the end zone with 1:25 left.
Barnhart then intercepted Hercher a second time with 46 seconds remaining to cement the Warriors' win.
"They were poised," Griffith said of his team. "Mikey made some plays. All the receivers made some plays. Dustin Blue was unbelievable (16 carries, season-high 101 yards)."
Then there was Barnhart.
"He's probably got one of our best football IQs on the team, and defensively makes a big difference out there for us," Griffith said of Barnhart. "The last two weeks he's been playing lights out. He's just going to keep getting better each week."
Queen Anne's linebacker Parker Whiteford set a school single-game record for tackles with 18, breaking the mark set by Kevin Morris in 2000.
Easton defeated Queen Anne's 21-14 in the Class 2A East Region semifinals in 2014, when Jaelon Moaney hit Dre' Stevens with a 41-yard touchdown pass with 2 minutes left.

Bennett.
Easton improved to 6-2, strengthening its hold on the No. 2 seed in the approaching Class 2A East playoffs behind undefeated and defending Class 2A state champion Stephen Decatur (8-0).

title: Burnham has Vikings seemingly in all the right places
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Burnham has Vikings seemingly in all the right places

 October 25, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports

 Rob Burnham deflects praise quite nicely."We got great kids. I'm not a good coach," Cambridge-South Dorchester High's first-year head football coach said. "All I've done is put people in places to be successful. I haven't done anything fancy."
Well, after Thursday night's 42-0 road victory at Washington, the Vikings have a fancy 8-0 record — the first time they've been unbeaten this deep into a season since 2000.
Despite his self evaluation, Burnham has proven to be a pretty good head coach, and has certainly put his personnel in the right spots offensively, as Cambridge-SD has outscored its last five opponents, 187-14.
Leading that charge has been junior running back Sterling Perkins, who has rushed for 902 yards and 10 touchdowns, and senior quarterback Anthony Hughes, who has 733 yards and a team-high 12 touchdowns on the ground, and has completed over 50% of his passes for 355 yards and seven touchdowns — two of those coming Thursday against the Jaguars.
But the Vikings have been equally, if not more impressive, on defense.
"The defense is definitely the strength of our team without question," Burnham said of a unit that has four players — KaMarii Stanley, Christen Dockins, Antonio Blueford and Tabrion Watts — with over 40 tackles apiece.
Hard to argue that considering Cambridge-SD has surrendered just one offensive touchdown over its last five games — that coming on an 8-yard run by Wicomico — and has shut out three of its last five opponents, including its last two.
"We've done pretty well defensively holding people," Burnham said. "Our kids play fast. We tackle well and drive the pile backwards. And we run fast to it."
That unit figures to face its stiffest test of the season next Friday when longtime rival Easton (5-2) comes to Cambridge for the regular-season finale for both teams.
"Easton brings a quality opponent to Cambridge next week," Burnham said. "They have some talent on offense that's pretty special and we have to be able to contain that. Our kids are going to be ready to play."
Burnham liked the way his team started for the most part against winless Washington. The Vikings scored on their first possession, committed a turnover, then scored the next three times they had the ball while building a 35-0 halftime lead.
Hughes was an efficient 4 of 5 passing for 65 yards and two touchdowns before being relieved by Nathan Twilley, who also had a scoring toss. Blueford, Ra'Quan Cornish and Tamyron Evans each had touchdown receptions, and William Jackson and Watts had one rushing touchdown apiece.
Still, Burnham said there's work to be done offensively.
"We have things we need to clean up offensively," Burnham said. "We're not anywhere near where I want to be offensively.
"Overall we blocked well. We finished well," Burnham said of Thursday's win. "But we have not played a complete game yet."

title: Rival clashes feature various degrees of confidence
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Rival clashes feature various degrees of confidence

 October 29, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports

 They each come into rivalry week with varying degrees of confidence.After getting shutout by defending Class 2A state champion Stephen Decatur on Oct. 11, Kent Island High's football team rides a two-game win streak into Friday's annual clash with county rival Queen Anne's.
The Lions come into Friday having won five of six, their latest, a 21-20 victory over Parkside eight days after losing a one-point heartbreaker to Easton.
Streaking Colonel Richardson readies for its annual duel with North Caroline having outscored its last four opponents, 203-20.
And though they are still searching for their first win of the season, the Bulldogs fell just two points shy of Kent Island but have senior star Zymear Smith back and running.
"I can see some progress that we've made," said Heath Wilkins, who became North Caroline's head coach just four weeks ago. "I wish I had the team for more time, but I don't, so this is what we've got."
For the second time in Wilkins' three games as head coach, the Bulldogs (0-8) held a halftime lead last Friday. Corey Bunce's 4-yard touchdown run and Caden Deavers' two-point conversion run gave North Caroline an 8-0 lead on Kent Island, which had a field-goal attempt blocked before the half.
But the Bucs (5-3) rebounded in the second half, as Nathan Green scored on runs of 14 and 38 yards to help push Kent Island to a 16-8 lead.
Caroline pulled within 16-14, when Bunce connected with tight end Declan Egan for a short touchdown pass in the fourth quarter. But the Bucs stopped North Caroline short on the two-point try, then picked up a couple of first downs over the final 4 minutes to melt the clock and seal the win.
"I think we've taken some steps," said Kent Island first-year head coach Zach Davis, who got a 16-carry, 123-yard rushing effort from Jaxson Hess against the Bulldogs. "We've been a streaky team; win three, lose three, and then we've won two.
"This team has been a work in progress, figuring out how do we have success because a lot of these guys are new starters," Davis added. "We bring back a ton of starters next year. But we're a young football team. Those growing pains showed in the middle of the season. We're getting better and that's what you want to see."
Queen Anne's head coach Brian Mooney has learned a lot about pain this season after losing a slew of starters to injuries, and then falling to Easton, 27-26, when Mikey O'Connor hit Chase Raab with a late touchdown pass on a fourth-and-five.
"The Easton game was a gut punch," Mooney said.
But it was the Lions delivering the gut punch last Friday by way of a 21-20 victory over Parkside.
Down 7-0, Queen Anne's (5-3) pulled even on John Connolly's 28-yard touchdown run in the second quarter. The Rams moved back in front in the third quarter, but again Connolly (season-high 27 carries, 156 yards rushing) answered, scoring on a 3-yard run. But Parkside maintained a slim lead when the Lions missed the point-after attempt.
Parkside extended its lead to 20-13 on a 70-yard touchdown pass. The Lions again looked poised to respond, only to fumble the ball away inside the Rams' 5-yard line. But Queen Anne's senior linebacker Parker Whiteford came through with one of the season's biggest plays when he made a tackle for a safety, drawing the Lions with 20-15.
Aided by Ja'Dereon Thompson's 33-yard completion to Jamison Woodward, Queen Anne's drove 60 yards, with Thompson scoring on a 4-yard run with a little over a minute to play giving the Lions a 21-20 victory.
"It was a nail-biter for sure," Mooney said. "It's huge. A confidence booster. Just again the resiliency. But we're going to scratch and claw just like we have all year."
Though is took a little while, Colonel Richardson appears to have found its groove.
Ja'Zir Dickerson carried 10 times for 175 yards and three touchdowns, and Derrick Mitchell had 100 yards on 11 touches during last Friday's 44-0 rout of Kent County, the Colonels' fourth straight win.
"We coach them each week to stay true to themselves and follow the system that we run," said Colonel head coach James Jackson, his team now 5-3. "Our backs I feel like are finally starting to follow our linemen, not trying to kick out too soon, or over-run the hole."
While the Colonel's running attack has impressed over the past four weeks, so has its defense, notching a pair of shutouts.
"Can we be better? Yes," Jackson said. "I think we need better play from our two d-tackles. Our d-ends have to contain a little better. Our linebackers, we've got to flow a little better. But the last four weeks they've been bent but they haven't been broken."

title: Hughes, Vikings rally past Warriors
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Hughes, Vikings rally past Warriors

 November 1, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports

 CAMBRIDGE — His first touchdown run evened the score in the second quarter.His second TD trimmed the home team's deficit in the third.
But it was Anthony Hughes' final touchdown run — a 11-yard sweep around right end with 4 minutes, 23 seconds remaining — that put Cambridge-South Dorchester High's football team ahead to stay Friday night, as the Vikings rallied for a 27-24 victory over longtime rival Easton to cap an undefeated regular season.
Cambridge-SD (9-0) will be the No. 1 seed in the Class 1A East Region playoffs and have a first-round bye. Easton (6-3) slipped to the No. 3 seed in the Class 2A East postseason, and will host No. 6 Parkside on Thursday night in the first round.
"Anthony is an absolute dog," Viking first-year head coach Rob Burnham said in praise of his senior quarterback. "He is so physical. He plays outside linebacker and quarterback for crying out loud. I think he tapped out on me for two snaps because he was tired.
"I'm so proud of him," Burnham continued of Hughes. "His growth as a player from a ninth grader when he came up to play for us as as young kid to now is absolutely tremendous."
Burnham's stress level may have been reaching the tremendous range in the first half, when the Vikings committed three fumbles — two leading to Easton touchdowns.
The Warriors recovered a third fumble when Jordan Horsey stripped the ball from Sterling Perkins at Easton's 2-yard line late in the second quarter. Easton could not convert that miscue into points.
The Warriors led 21-14 at halftime, and had a chance to widen that lead when it recovered a fourth Vikings' fumble on the second-half kickoff. Easton drove to the Cambridge-SD 7. But on third-and-goal, Cambridge-SD's Majestic Jones stepped in front of Warrior receiver Chase Raab and intercepted Easton quarterback Mikey O'Connor's pass in the end zone, keeping it a seven-point game.
On the very next play, the Vikings lost their fifth fumble on their 20-yard line. The Warriors pushed to the Cambridge-SD 9, where they settled for Dominic Stanco's 26-yard field goal and a 24-14 lead with 8:55 left in the third quarter.
But Easton wouldn't score the rest of the game.
"We had opportunities to put them away, to increase the gap," Easton head coach Matt Griffith said. "We failed to do that. When you do that against a good team this is what happens. It comes back and bites you."
Easton got the ball back after a Vikings' three-and-out. But on second down, Jayden Hollowell intercepted O'Connor, giving the Vikings possession on their 44.
Back-to-back false starts pushed Cambridge-SD back to its 34, where on first-and-20, Hughes found a seam and trucked 66 yards for a touchdown, drawing the Vikings within 24-20 with 6:28 left in the third quarter. Cambridge-SD bobbled the snap on the point-after attempt, and tried a pass, but was called for intentional grounding.
Kimir Lake picked off O'Connor to end Easton's next possession, but the Warriors forced a punt and carried their four-point lead into the fourth quarter.
Easton looked ready to potentially add to its lead driving from its 25 to the Vikings 26. But on second-and-10 Lake intercepted O'Connor again and returned the ball to the Warrior 40. Hughes had runs of 8, 7 and 17 yards before turning the corner for an 11-yard touchdown run with 4:23 left. Collin Bair's point-after kick made it 27-24.
"I got to get it," said Hughes when asked what he was thinking on his final scoring run. "I've got to do it for my coach, my line. My teammates trust me so I got to go do it for them."
Easton punted on its next drive. Cambridge-SD kept the ball in Hughes' hands for the better part of the final minutes before punting the ball back to Easton with 34.7 seconds left. But the Warriors couldn't mount a last threat, as Brady Walls' fourth-down heave was intercepted by Lake. Hughes took a knee to end the game.
Easton took a 7-0 lead when O'Connor hit Raab with a 27-yard touchdown pass and Stanco hit the PAT with 9:56 left in the first quarter.
Cambridge-SD answered, as Perkins was sprung for a 55-yard touchdown run. Bair's extra point tied the game 7-all with 8:53 to go in the first.
The Warriors capitalized on a Vikings fumble, as O'Connor scored on a 2-yard run for a 14-7 lead with 38.2 second left in the first quarter.
Hughes responded with a 58-yard touchdown run just 52 seconds into the second quarter to tie the game at 14-14.
"He's good," Griffith said of Hughes. "We knew coming in he's good. (Number) One and two (Perkins), very, very good. They're a load to tackle. Two is very shifty. One is just a man."
Easton moved back in front with 7:17 left in the second quarter on O'Connor's 8-yard touchdown run.
"Our defense is pretty stout," Burnham said. "I think that's the most offensive points we've given up on the season. The O'Connor kid, he's a tremendous football player. Coach Griffith had a great game plan. They did a lot of really good things in the box, attacking downfield with switch routes and different combinations. And I would not want to play them again. I'm glad they're in the 2A and we're in the 1A because I don't want any part of the Easton Warriors right now."

title: Blue, O'Connor lead Easton
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Blue, O'Connor lead Easton

 November 8, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports

 EASTON — Matt Griffith delivered a familiar coaching lament."We still haven't played a full game," Easton High's head football coach said. "And if we can ever figure that out before the season ends we're going to be OK."
Well, the Warriors figured out one thing Thursday night — how to win a home playoff game.
Dustin Blue and Mikey O'Connor each rushed for three touchdowns, and Jordan Horsey had an interception and returned a second takeaway for a touchdown, as Easton won a playoff game on its home turf for the first time since 1993 with a 62-36 victory over Parkside in a Class 2A East Region first-round game.
The third-seeded Warriors (7-3) advance to the second round, where they will play at No. 2 seed Kent Island (7-3) at a date yet to be determined.
"We had more turnovers than they did," said Parkside head coach Brendan Riley, whose team committed three turnovers and had a punt blocked, leading to 24 Easton points.
The Warriors had four turnovers in a 37-30 loss to the Rams on Oct. 11. Thursday they had none.
"They came into our house and beat us," O'Connor said of the Oct. 11 loss. "So we had like a chip on our shoulder. And the fact that we haven't won a home playoff game in a long time."
There were plenty of other reasons why Easton notched its first home playoff win since a 35-15 victory over Smithsburg in a 1993 Class 1A quarterfinal.
Blue was a battering ram, carrying 24 times for 125 yards — both season highs — and three touchdowns, and also caught four passes for 33 yards and another TD.
"Dustin and the o-line. I believe that group and Dustin really controlled the game," O'Connor said. "They carried us."
O'Connor wasn't too shabby either. The senior quarterback carried 18 times for 92 yards and three touchdowns, and completed 13 of 19 passes for 165 yards and a touchdown.
"Everything is centered on Mikey," Riley said. "I think he does a good job of commanding what they do."
Horsey intercepted Parkside quarterback Chris Morandi on the fourth play from scrimmage, setting the Warriors up at the Rams' 5-yard line. Four plays later, Blue crashed through the middle for a 1-yard touchdown. Dominic Stanco, who was 8 for 8 on extra-point attempts, and booted field goals of 24 and 36 yards, tacked on the PAT for a 7-0 Easton lead with 8:39 left in the first quarter.
The sixth-seeded Rams (3-7), who had not won since their win at Easton, pulled within 7-6, when Morandi connected with Tavian Dashiell for a 79-yard touchdown pass with 3:47 to go in the first quarter. The Warriors maintained the lead though, when Logan Friend blocked the extra point.
Easton answered with an 11-play, 65-yard march that ended with Blue blasting in from the 1 with 25 seconds remaining in the first quarter.
"He ran the ball unbelievable tonight," Griffith said of Blue. "Very hard. Very committed. We knew coming in we wanted to pound the rock with him. He did exactly what we asked him to do: ball security. He was able to pick us up short yards and stuff. And he extended some big runs in the middle, taking advantage of some of the alignments they gave us."
Less than 4 minutes into the second quarter, Rams senior running back Karontez Bratten (24 carries, 240 yards) scored on a 2-yard run. James Harmon's two-point run tied the game at 14-all.
But Friend gave the Warriors another short field when he blocked a punt. Parkside's punter kicked the ball out of bounds, giving Easton a safety. But Griffith opted to give up the points in favor of getting the ball at the Rams' 2-yard line. O'Connor scored on a 2-yard run with 5:20 left, then watched Stanco drill a 24-yard field goal as time ran out in the first half with Easton up 24-14.
The Warriors widened their lead to 31-14 on their first possession of the second half, as O'Connor rolled left and dumped a short pass to Blue for a 12-yard touchdown.
But Bratten, who had five touchdowns and rushed for 248 yards on 23 touches in the first meeting, broke free for a 59-yard touchdown jaunt and ran in the two-point conversion, shaving Easton's lead to 31-22 with 6:45 to go in the third.
"Is he a senior," Griffith asked of Bratten. "I hope he is. I hope he's graduating and moving out of the country or something. He's a dude. He's good. We were in a lot of the right places and he just made us miss. We'd hit him and he'd bounce off. Unbelievable."
Easton came right back though, as Blue, who bounced off defenders all game, scored on an 18-yard run around the right side, extending the Warrior lead to 38-22 with 4:12 still left in the third.
"Before the game, I expected the ball 30 times," Blue said. "But just doing it for the seniors. I just love 'em so much, and I just want to keep playing with them on and on. So I'm just going to put it all on the field every single week."
Parkside wouldn't go away, as Harmon's 6-yard touchdown run and two-pointer trimmed the Rams' deficit to 38-30 with 2:50 left in the third.
The Warriors though took control from there, scoring the next 24 points.
O'Connor's 1-yard touchdown run made it 45-30 with 1:17 left in the third. Kyree Acree intercepted Morandi on the first play of the fourth quarter, setting up Stanco's 36-yard field goal for an 18-point cushion. O'Connor was sprung for a 17-yard touchdown run, moving Easton to a 55-30 lead.
Horsey then ended Parkside's next possession, when he stripped the ball from Bratten and raced 41 yards for a touchdown and a 62-30 lead.
Bratten added a 40-yard touchdown run with 2:12 left for the final score.
Easton's 62 points were the most it scored in a playoff game in at least 46 years.

 AMERICAN CORNER — James Jackson had no explanation."This is new to me," Colonel Richardson High's head football coach said of the seemingly new-found speed of Bradley Thomas.
Thomas also struggled to provide any further insight.
"I don't know," Thomas said of his surprising higher gear. "All my brothers are linemen so I have no clue where it came from. I guess I was gifted differently."
Thomas ran for a pair of touchdowns, including a 75-yard sprint late in the first half, and also returned a fumble for a touchdown Friday night to help the Colonels rout Snow Hill, 51-6, in the first round of the Class 1A East Region playoffs.
Fourth-seeded Colonel Richardson (6-4) advances to next week's second round, where it will travel to unbeaten No. 1 seed Cambridge-South Dorchester (9-0).
"I told them in the locker room, 'It's hard beating a team twice,'" said Jackson, whose team defeated the Eagles 43-6 in Snow Hill on Oct. 11. "'We got to go out, we got to score quickly. And then don't let up.' When we scored on that first drive I reminded the offensive linemen, 'Hey, we're not done, so don't go out on our next drive and lay an egg.'"
The Colonels didn't, scoring on all four of their first-half possessions for a 32-0 halftime cushion. Colonel also scored the only two times it had the ball in the second half before Thomas' 9-yard fumble return for a touchdown made it 51-0 with with 5 minutes remaining.
Fifth-seeded Snow Hill (5-5) avoided a shutout, when Justin Shipley returned a kickoff 95 yards down the visitors' sideline for a touchdown in the closing minutes.
Winners of five of their last six games, Colonel pieced together a 13-play, 70-yard scoring drive to open the game that included an 18-yard burst on fourth down by Thomas, and ended with quarterback Tarron Hammond's 5-yard touchdown run. Thomas ran in the two-point conversion for an 8-0 lead with 4 minutes, 44 seconds left in the first half.
The Colonels blew the game open with a 24-point second quarter. Derrick Mitchell scored on a 16-yard run and ran in the two-point try for a 16-0 lead on the first play of the quarter. Thomas bulled in from a yard out and Collin Brewer powered in the two-point run to make it 24-0 with 7:13 left before halftime.
"He started the year as a backup quarterback and fullback," Jackson said of Thomas. "And then we were like, 'You know what? Maybe we should try Bradley at some wing.' He's a bruiser. We got two finesse running backs so we decided we need a pounder and he became that pounding back. Brings back that (Camron) Gondeck that we used to have (at running back)."
Snow Hill drove to the Colonel 11 on its next drive, but fumbled on a fourth-and-one. Three plays later, Thomas found open space on the left side and romped 75 yards for a touchdown with his jubilant head coach chasing him down the sideline.
"I was excited for him," Jackson said smiling. "This is something you don't see with him. Usually he'll give you 10 to 15 yards, but when he breaks a long one it's exciting. I thought he really ran out of gas the last five yards, but he made it in.
"Tonight the way he ran the football, it was good to see," Jackson continued. "The long runs he had tonight were impressive. He's not a speed guy. When I get in the locker room I'm going to ask him was he running scared, or has he found some speed somewhere."
Thomas finished with 168 yards on 10 carries.
"I just saw green," Thomas said of his 75-yard scoring dash. "I was like, 'Just keep going. Don't fumble the ball. Just keep going.' And I kept going."
Hammond's 26-yard touchdown pass to Carter Tubitt, and Morgan Demir's point-after kick with 5:30 remaining in the third quarter pushed Colonel's lead to 39-0, and started the running clock.
Thomas then intercepted quarterback Dominic Kuipers on Snow Hill's next play from scrimmage, stirring Colonel's biggest sideline celebration of the night. The Colonels were back in the end zone two plays later, with Dominque Caven sweeping 28 yards around right end ffor a 45-0 lead.
Thomas capped Colonel's scoring two plays later when he grabbed a fumble and ran nine yards for his third touchdown of the game.

title: Stakes raised in 2nd meeting between CSD, Colonel
author: Bill Haufe

Stakes raised in 2nd meeting between CSD, Colonel

 November 13, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 It was more of an announcement than analysis."That just wasn't us," Colonel Richardson High head football coach James Jackson said of his team's 23-0 loss at Cambridge-South Dorchester on Sept. 27.
Jackson wasn't disrespecting or discrediting the Vikings, though his reaction was certainly understandable considering a week earlier, the Colonels put up 33 points while flirting with an upset of Kent Island. Since that loss to the Vikings — the only time they've been shut out all year — the Colonels have won five of six in lopsided fashion.
The latest of those romps came last week during a 51-6 rout of Snow Hill, which propelled the fourth-seeded Colonels (6-4) into Friday's 6 p.m. rematch at top-seeded Cambridge-SD (9-0) in a Class 1A East second-round playoff game.
"It's always tough to beat a team twice in the same season," Vikings first-year head coach Rob Burnham said. "I expect coach Jackson to have a solid game plan. I expect his kids to come out and play hard. And I expect the game to be more competitive than it was last time. And it's our job to make sure that it's not as competitive."
Colonel had one turnover and about half a dozen fumbled snaps from center in that Week 4 loss. But Jackson noted his team's biggest problem that first meeting was "from our (offensive) line not knowing who to block. So correcting them, that changed a lot."
Those changes have helped running back Derrick Mitchell gain a team-high 800 yards and score five touchdowns on 94 carries. Ja'Zir Dickerson, back after missing the last two games, has rushed for 774 yards and 11 touchdowns on 72 touches.
"After the Cambridge game, the running backs got a better understanding of hitting the holes," Jackson said. "You can't overrun the holes and you can't assume just because you see the flash of a jersey that the hole is clogged. You've got to stay patient and run behind your linemen."
There has also been the emergence of Bradley Thomas (41-425, 3 TDs), who carried 10 times for 168 yards and two touchdowns during last week's first-round playoff against Snow Hill.
"We didn't use Bradley much at wing when we played them last time," Jackson said. "I think having Bradley this game will give us a little more power."
Colonel also has quarterback Tarron Hammond, who has run for six touchdowns, and completed 19 of 37 passes for 662 yards, nine TDs and no interceptions.
And while Colonel has improved, it still faces one of the Bayside Conference's most athletic and fastest defenses.
"I'm glad we don't have to block ourselves," Burnham said of his defense, which like Colonel logged three shutouts this season. "Our kids run fast across the board and they pursue to the football. And we preach it in practice and we drill it. And we try to be technicians and do the little things well."
Sophomore K'Marion Hall, who was injured in the first Colonel game, returns to the defensive line, and will play tight end for an offense that has the potential to score on any down from anywhere.
"Well, those kids that run fast for us on defense also run fast for us on offense," Burnham said.
Leading the offense is Anthony Hughes, who has been a problem for everyone he's faced this season. The senior quarterback, who also plays outside linebacker, has carried 108 times for 957 yards and 15 touchdowns, and completed 34 of 64 passes for 413 yards and seven touchdowns. Then there is Sterling Perkins Jr., who has rushed for 1,047 yards and 11 touchdowns on 105 touches.
"The first thing we've got to do is limit their explosive plays," Jackson said. "We can't give up the big runs. You can't let a kid catch a 7-yard slant and turn it into a 50-yard run."
Jackson is also well aware of how Hughes and Perkins can shed and break tackles in an instant.
"You got to wrap up," Jackson said. "And if you got him wrapped up, we can't assume that one person is going to bring either one of them down. We talk about that all the time: gang tackling. And don't assume someone's down. Somebody's got to come in and clean up."
Burnham, who's never coached a team that had a first-round bye in the playoffs, said his team is healthy and doesn't expect the Vikings to be rusty.
"We want to score as fast as we can," Burnham said. "But they are not going to roll over for us. They have a bunch of seniors and they don't want it to be their last game. And we have a bunch of seniors that don't want it to be their last game."

Warriors, Bucs set for round two

 Last Friday's 41-0 rout of James M. Bennett, was the first time Kent Island High head football coach Zach Davis had played an opponent twice in one season.Matt Griffith has seen the same team a handful of times during his two stints as Easton High's head coach. During that span, Griffith has watched his team lose to a 2A rival in the regular season then beat that same team in the postseason. He's also been on the flip side of that scenario.
So it's no surprise heading into Friday's 6 p.m. Class 2A East Region second-round playoff clash with the Buccaneers at Andy Schipul Stadium, that Griffith hasn't placed much stock in the Warriors' 43-24 victory over Kent Island on Sept. 27.
"Game one doesn't mean anything except they know a little bit about us, and we know a little bit about them," Griffith said. "That's it."
Second-seeded Kent Island (7-3) enters the game on a four-game win streak. The third-seeded Warriors (7-3) opened the season with a four-game win streak, and arrive for this second encounter having won three of their last four.
"I think myself and my coaches have done a nice job of keeping them level, knowing that we're playing a really good football team that's coached very well, and that there's going to be adjustments and changes," Griffith said. "We have to be able to respond to that and be able to play our brand of football. And hopefully we have a better night than they do."
Adjustments figure to be coming from both sides.
Kent Island will look to contain Easton quarterback Mikey O'Connor, who rushed for 250 yards and three touchdowns, and passed for 146 yards and two touchdowns in the first game. The Warriors will again hope to limit the Bucs' two-pronged running attack of Jaxson Hess, who has carried 157 times this season for 987 yards and nine touchdowns, and Nate Green (101-825-9).
As far as wholesale changes?
"You have some wrinkles, but you can't change who you are," said Davis, who spent nine seasons coaching in West Virginia before taking over at Kent Island this year. "You can't put in a whole new playbook. But you have some things that they haven't seen on tape and just hope your guys play well, get them ready to play."
After losing 52-0 to defending 2A state champion Stephen Decatur, Kent Island has reeled off four straight wins, outscoring its opponents 122-35, which has led Davis to think his team has found its identity.
"We've embraced what kind of football works for us," Davis said. "We are blue collar. We play old-school football. That's the style of football I prefer to play; I think our staff prefers to play. That's what we want to do. We want to be hard-nosed, have a hard edge. And we want to get the game to the fourth quarter because that's where we feel we are the best."
Offensively, that means running the ball with Hess and Green.
"Kent Island has some really good running backs," Griffith said. "Number 11 (Green) is fast and very strong and athletic. Twenty-two (Hess) is what I consider one of the better running backs in the Bayside (Conference) as well. He hits the hole hard. He's a powerful runner.
"What they do they do very well," Griffith added. "We're going to be challenged and have to tackle well, and do our jobs up front to give our skill guys opportunities to make plays for us."
Easton also has to be concerned with quarterback Gavan Henry (38 carries, 142 yards, 7 touchdowns), who completed 35 of 94 for 607 yards and seven touchdowns — two coming against the Warriors — and his top target Jackson Towers (8 receptions, 207 yards, 2 touchdowns).
O'Connor figures to again be the focal point for the Bucs' defense. The senior has thrown for 1,761 yards and 19 touchdowns, and rushed for 1,005 yards and 16 TDs. He also has an array of targets with Chase Raab (519 yards, 8 touchdowns), Colin Mooney (388-4), Diontaye Copper (339-5), Carter Mooney (304-1) and Zach Barnhart.
But the Warriors were aided greatly in last Thursday's 62-36 first-round win over Parkside by junior running back Dustin Blue (579 yards), who last week ran for 125 yards and three touchdowns, and also had a touchdown reception.
"I think Mikey and Dustin, they offset each other and complement each other very well," Griffith said. "And I think that's part of what's taken place now. Mikey might have done some things earlier in the season that people want to take away now, and that allows Dustin to be able to showcase his ability. He's always been a very good running back for us and he's going to get some more opportunities based on what teams do against us."
Griffith has called his offensive line a work in progress throughout the season, but has seen improvement. He knows that unit will again have to play well in Friday's round two.
"We're going up against a really good defensive front," Griffith said. "They're going to have to have a really good game if we're going to be successful. Defensively, they're going to give us multiple looks, they're going to bring pressure. We've got to control the football. And we've got to take what they give us and not force things. One of the things that we had a lot of success with the first time is we didn't get silly trying to force things."
Execution and limiting turnovers and penalties have been stressed by both coaching staffs since the preseason. But Davis thinks if he and the Bucs are to even the slate against Easton they will have to stay true to their identity.
"We got to be able to run the football and stop the run," Davis said. "We rush for over 200 yards and we win. That's what we're going to try to do on offense. On defense, if we can hold them to 100 yards or less rushing, we're going to win. That's what we want to do."

 STEVENSVILLE — Kent Island High head football coach Zach Davis has seen enough of Mikey O'Connor."I'm glad he graduates," Davis said of Easton High's senior quarterback. "He basically beat us by himself. I told him before the game, I thought he was a great player. And he showed it tonight."
O'Connor ran for two touchdowns and threw for two, including a 43-yard connection to Diontaye Copper with 2 minutes, 15 seconds remaining Friday night, as the third-seeded Warriors defeated the No. 2 seed Buccaneers, 28-21, in a Class 2A East Region second-round playoff at Andy Schipul Stadium.
After going 1-9 a year ago, Easton is 8-3 and now awaits for the state tournament to be re-seeded for next weekend's state quarterfinals.
"We didn't score the whole second half," said O'Connor, whose 3-yard touchdown run with 1:17 left in the first half helped Easton to a 21-14 halftime lead. "They were really stopping us and we were just thinking, 'First down. Next first down.' So we were taking it one play at a time. And when you do that, you put a bunch of good plays together, and you bust one, that really turned the tide."
After a scoreless third quarter, Kent Island (7-4) tied the game 4 seconds into the fourth quarter on quarterback Gavan Henry's 1-yard sneak. Spencer Chappell's point-after kick tied the game at 21-all.
Easton's ensuing possession ended with a fourth-down incompletion. Kent Island punted the next time it had the ball.
The Warriors took possession at their 20-yard line with 6:17 remaining. On third-and-11, O'Connor hit Colin Mooney for an 11-yard pick-up and a first down. Five consecutive O'Connor runs set up a third-and-five at the Bucs' 43. O'Connor hit Copper on an out route, then watched his receiver cut toward the middle of the field and outrun everyone into the end zone for a 27-21 lead. Dominic Stanco drilled his fourth straight point after for a 28-21 Easton lead.
"You try to stop him running the football and he throws on you," Davis said of O'Connor.
Kent Island got the ball back on its 37 with 2:15 left. As the Bucs lined up on first down, Easton called time to make a defensive adjustment. On the next play, Copper intercepted Henry, giving the Warriors the ball at the Kent Island 49 with 2:09 left.
"Luckily for us we were able to make one more big play than Kent Island tonight, on both sides of the ball," Easton head coach Matt Griffith said. "Big drive. Drove down and scored with like 2:15 left. And then get a huge pick. Call a timeout to see the formation, made a quick adjustment on our coverage, and, man, played it perfect."
O'Connor picked up two first downs to kill the remaining 2:09, cementing the victory.
"They came through when they needed to and that was at the most important time," O'Connor said of his offensive line. "When we got those first downs, it was all them. Like I didn't get touched literally until I had the first down."
Easton took a 7-0 lead, when O'Connor busted loose around right end for a 41-yard touchdown just over 2 minutes into the game. Stanco added the PAT.
Kent Island fumbled on its first play of the game, giving Easton the ball on the Bucs 45. The Warriors drove to the Bucs' 13, setting up Stanco's 30-yard field goal attempt that drifted wide right.
Henry's 1-yard sneak and Chappell's extra-point tied the game at 7-7 with 32 seconds left in the first quarter.
The Warriors moved back ahead with 8:50 to go in the second quarter, when O'Connor hit Mooney with a 23-yard touchdown pass in the left, front corner of end zone for a 14-7 lead.
The Bucs again pulled even, as Nate Green was sprung for an 11-yard touchdown run with 2:26 to go before halftime.
Easton responded. Dustin Blue broke free on a 50-yard run on his first carry. O'Connor carried for 12 yards and then raced around left end and squeezed down the sideline for the go-ahead touchdown and a 21-14 halftime lead.

But with 1 minute, 15 seconds remaining, senior wide receiver Antonio Blueford made a leaping grab in the back of the end zone on Anthony Hughes' pass for the winning touchdown, lifting Cambridge-SD to a 14-7 victory.
The top-seeded Vikings (10-0) will host three-time defending Class 1A state champion Fort Hill (4-7) on Friday at 6:30 p.m. in a 1A state quarterfinal. The Sentinels, who forfeited five victories this season for using an ineligible player, outscored their two regional opponents by a combined 103-20.

"We showed we shouldn't have lost that game by 23 points. We should have been in that game, but we didn't play to our potential. So when we play to our potential I feel like we can play with anybody."
Cambridge-SD took a 7-0 lead in the first quarter when Hughes' broke up the middle for a touchdown run and Collin Bair tacked on the extra point.

title: Easton playing with familiar tag
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Easton playing with familiar tag

 Underdog.Easton High's football team started the season with that tag when it was ranked 10th in a preseason poll.
The Warriors steadily shedded that label through a 6-3 regular season, won two Class 2A East Regional playoffs, and are one of three Bayside Conference teams still playing along with defending 2A state champion Stephen Decatur and undefeated Cambridge-South Dorchester, the No. 1 seed in Class 1A.
Now, as it heads into Friday's Class 2A state quarterfinal at second-seeded Milford Mill (9-1) at 6:30 p.m., No. 7 seed Easton (8-3) returns to its familiar role.
"We know we're the underdog," Warrior head coach Matt Griffith said. "And we love it. And while we're happy with a lot of things we've done this year, we're not done. We have a lot of work still to do.
"Yes, we're playing a very good football team," Griffith said of the Millers, who won the 2A state title two years ago then lost in last year's state semifinals to eventual state champ Decatur. "Yes, they're very athletic. Yes, they're big. Yes, they're fast. We're focused on not who's the toughest, but who can be the toughest the longest. We need to be able to take their punches early and be able to respond. And if we can do that I like our chances, if we can keep it close at the end of the game."
If the Warriors are to keep it close, they will have to limit a Millers team that scored 32 or more points in eight of their nine victories this season.
Leading the way is junior quarterback Owen Newberns, who has completed 88 of 140 passes for 1,586 yards, 18 touchdowns and just four interceptions. Easton's secondary figures to be challenged by receivers Romero Ison (33 receptions, 534 yards, five touchdowns) and Derrell Pierson (23-497-6). Then there's running back Damon Ferguson, who has carried 72 times for 975 yards and 12 touchdowns.
"Each team is different because they have a different formula for winning," Milford Mill head coach Reggie White said. "It's really cool to coach these different types of teams. One year you may have a running team. One year you may have a passing team. One year you might have a ferocious defense.
"So this year's team, we've got some guys who are very, very athletic," White continued. "We've got some guys who can break a game open. It's the little nuances that you try to lean on during the game to help you win."
The Millers also have the biggest offensive line the Warriors have faced all year,
"Their center is like 6-(foot)-6, 320," Griffith said. "They run tight zone and outside zone really, really well. They got a really fast running back. Their quarterback is super athletic and he can throw the deep ball to receivers who are really athletic."
Easton has a really athletic quarterback of its own in senior Mikey O'Connor, who has completed 123 of 228 passes for 1,908 yards, 21 touchdowns and 14 interceptions, and also run for 1,247 yards and 18 touchdowns on 186 carries.
"The first thing has to start with the signal-caller, their quarterback," White said when asked his biggest concerns with Easton. "He's a lefty. He's different. He has it. And I know about the O-line. They might be young, but they'll fight you."
That young front will look to open avenues for not only O'Connor, but junior running back Dustin Blue, who has carried 107 times for 632 yards and seven touchdowns.
The Warriors also have a fleet of receivers, which include Chase Raab (24 receptions, 519 yards, 8 touchdowns) and Diontaye Copper (21-382-6), who had the winning touchdown catch in last Friday's 28-21 second-round win over Kent Island. O'Connor's other targets are Colin Mooney (32-452-5), Carter Mooney (16-304-1) and Zach Barnhart (10-115-1).
"They're very athletic on defense," Griffith said of Milford Mill. "They're overly aggressive at times, which we're hoping we can take advantage of, and try to be a little patient in how we do things. Try to make them uncomfortable. No one's really made them uncomfortable this year except Loyola-(Blakefield), who beat them."
The Warriors, who have won four of their last five, also have to continue protecting the football. They have committed just one turnover in their last two games.
White also noted keeping mistakes to a minimum.
"I think our biggest obstacle is when we look in the mirror; it's ourselves sometimes," White said. "We're just trying to eliminate mental errors and play a whole game."

Vikings face Fort Hill in quarterfinals instead of title bout

 With the exception of a few injuries, and the assorted turnovers and penalties that leave coaches muttering, the season has gone pretty much as planned for Cambridge-South Dorchester High's football team."We had talked all season," first-year Vikings' head coach Rob Burnham said, "about doing the things we're supposed to do, and being successful, and work hard, and improve day after day. Get through the season undefeated. Get the number one overall seed in the (Class) 1A, and then we won't play the Sentinels until we go to Annapolis. Obviously, things changed on that."
Cambridge-SD did go undefeated during the regular season and earned the No. 1 overall seed when the state playoffs were reseeded last week.
As for meeting three-time defending 1A state champion Fort Hill in a potential state-title showdown in Annapolis? Well, that changed when the Sentinels forfeited five regular-season games for using an ineligible player. Fort Hill remained eligible for the postseason though, romped to a pair of regional victories, and come into Friday's 6:30 p.m. state quarterfinal at Cambridge-SD (10-0) as the No. 8 seed at 4-7.
"I met with our guys and said, 'Obviously the circumstances have changed and what we worked hard for isn't necessarily going to be given to us,'" Burnham said. "'We still have to go out and take it. So in order to get what we want we have to beat them. We just have to do it two weeks earlier than we had planned on.'"
A Cambridge-SD assistant last year, Burnham and Fort Hill head coach Zack Alkire agreed this is not the same Sentinels team that routed the Vikings, 38-20, in last year's state semifinals in Cumberland.
"We have a much better shot to run the ball on them this year than last year," Burnham said. "I've coached for 26 years and that was the best high school team I've seen regardless of classification in three different states. They were really good."
But that team that went on to win a third straight state title while extending its winning streak to 21 games, graduated 20 players, and is not as senior heavy this year.
"We play 10 sophomores throughout the course of a game and they've done really well for us," Alkire said. "There's been some growing pains. But the seniors have shown good leadership and gotten those guys to get us to where we are today."
One thing hasn't changed though with the Sentinels.
"Still the same ground-and-pound style of offense," Alkire said. "We try to spread you out when we can, but it's mostly going to be under center, ground and pound."
Leading that rushing attack is senior running back Jabril Daniels, who has toted the ball 156 times for 1,664 yards and 26 touchdowns this season. Braelyn Younger (43-485-9) is also a threat. And though senior quarterback Nash Cassell, who has completed 13 of 27 passes for 276 yards and six touchdowns, isn't a huge running threat, Alkire said he "does a great job of getting the ball where it needs to be."
That offense faces one of the Bayside Conference's quickest defenses.
"They're very aggressive defensively; try to cause problems in your backfield," Alkire said of Cambridge-SD.
But Burnham knows the unit he's called the backbone of his team since August, faces perhaps its biggest test of the season.
"Fort Hill football is Fort Hill football," Burnham said. "They play physical. They play fast. They do multiple things offensively. They run the ball consistently with multiple backs. We have to contain their run, limit their explosive plays on defense."
Cambridge-SD also possesses big-play talent, with senior quarterback Anthony Hughes and senior running back Sterling Perkins Jr., who has gained over a 1,000 yards this season.
"Offensively, we need to protect the football and then be opportunistic and make plays when we can," Burnham said.
Though the Sentinels have usually been at home during the past three postseasons, Alkire said his team has adapted to playing on the road after the ineligibility ruling.
"Just a matter of getting the kids in the mindset to be able to go on the road and endure some of the longer road trips, and experience some of the things that opposing teams have had to experience against us," Alkire said. "It's been a transition but the kids have accepted it and they moved on."
And though its date with Fort Hill has come two weeks earlier than expected, Burnham thinks the Vikings are ready.
"I think our kids are excited about an opportunity to prove ourself on a big stage against a quality opponent," Burnham said. "In order to get where we want to be we have to beat them. To coin the phrase, 'To be the man you've got to beat the man.' They've been the man the last three years and we want to take it. So we have to win. That's how it is."

author: Bill Haufe
content:
Sentinels end Vikings' unbeaten run

 November 22, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports

 CAMBRIDGE — It was a great run.And for one half, it looked like top-seeded Cambridge-South Dorchester High's football team might extend that run, as it carried momentum and a six-point lead into the locker room.
But Fort Hill shut down the Vikings in the second half en route to a 30-12 come-from-behind victory Friday night in a Class 1A state quarterfinal played in a steady, wind-driven rain.
"Kids worked really hard. Coaches worked really hard," said Cambridge-SD head coach Rob Burnham, whose team finished the season 10-1. "Didn't end the way we wanted it to end. It hurts. It really does."
Eighth-seeded Fort Hill (5-7) took a 6-0 lead with just under 8 minutes left in the first quarter, when Jabril Daniels broke loose down the visitors' sideline for a 54-yard touchdown run. Jacob Bone's point-after kick was no good.
The Sentinels carried that 6-0 lead into the second quarter. But Cambridge-SD recovered a second Fort Hill fumble at the Vikings 46. Cambridge-SD quarterback Anthony Hughes hit Majestic Jones for a 20-yard gain to the Sentinels' 31. Six plays later, Hughes found Ka'Marii Stanley for an 8-yard touchdown pass. Fort Hill blocked Collin Bair's point-after attempt, leaving the score tied at 6-all with 4:44 remaining in the first half.
The three-time defending state champions lost a third fumble on their next possession that Hughes returned to the Fort Hill 15. The Sentinels defense stiffened. But on fourth-and-four, Hughes hit Antonio Blueford for a 9-yard touchdown pass and a 12-6 lead. Fort Hill was called for pass interference on the two-point attempt. Hughes tried running the two-point conversion in, but was stopped short.
"We had opportunities in the first half and we capitalized," Burnham said.
Despite being held to its lowest first-half point total in these playoffs, Fort Hill didn't panic.
"We weren't playing our style of football," Fort Hill head coach Zack Alkire said. "Lot of guys were down, probably feeling a bit sorry for themselves and we just tried to remind them that we're only down six points. It only takes one play to get going. And we got that one play early and we didn't stop from there."
Cambridge-SD took the second-half kickoff and gained a first down on an 18-yard carry by Sterling Perkins Jr. The Vikings went backwards from there, a low snap from center resulted in a 7-yard sack of Hughes on third down. The Vikings attempted to salvage a second low snap from center on the ensuing punt, but turned the ball over on downs, giving Fort Hill possession at the Cambridge-SD 16.
Daniels worked his way through the left side before reaching the ball across the goal for a 15-yard touchdown run. Bone kicked the extra point to give the Sentinels a 13-12 led with 9:24 to go in the third quarter.
A short kickoff return and an 8-yard sack of Hughes forced another Vikings' punt, giving Fort Hill another short field at the 35. The Sentinels moved 34 yards before Daniels scored on a 1-yard run on fourth-and-goal. Daniels' two-point run extended Fort Hill's lead to 21-12 with 2:13 left in the third quarter.
"Jabril's a tough player," Alkire said. "Jabril, he's all heart, he's all emotion. He was trying to put too much on his shoulders (in the first half). He was able to control himself a little better in the second half. Can't say enough great things about him. He's the leader of our team for sure."
Fort Hill widened its lead to 28-12 with 8:25 remaining when Braelyn Younger caught a 9-yard touchdown pass from Nash Cassell with 8:25 left.
On the ensuing kickoff, Cambridge-SD's Willie Jackson slipped at the 1-yard line. On the next play, Fort Hill's Noah House shot through the line and tackled Hughes for a safety and a 30-12 lead.
"Defense was great," Alkire said. "Defense was really good all night long. We gave up two cheap ones, but for the most part I thought we did a nice job all night long on defense."
Fort Hill killed almost 5 minutes of clock before turning the ball over on downs to the Vikings with 3:05 left. Hughes hit Perkins for a gain down to the Fort Hill 30. But the Vikings were flagged for an ineligible man downfield.
"We didn't make plays when we needed to," Burnham said. "They did."

title: EASTON TURNS IT AROUND
author: Bill Haufe
content:
EASTON TURNS IT AROUND

 November 26, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports

 It certainly wasn't the ending it was looking for.It was raining sideways and blowing hard, which neutralized the passing game really for both teams.
The opponent, Milford Mill, was big, talented, and two years removed from a state championship.
And the last thing Easton High's football team wanted to do was give the Millers extra opportunities via turnovers. But the seventh-seeded Warriors committed four turnovers during last Friday night's season-ending 42-7 loss to second-seeded Milford Mill in a Class 2A state quarterfinal.
"If we could have thrown the ball like we normally do, I think it's a little different," Easton head coach Matt Griffith said of a game that at one point was 13-7 in the first half. "I still think they beat us, but I think it's probably 42-21, 35-21, something like that.
"They're good," Griffith added of the Millers (10-1), who advance to Friday's semifinals, where they will host No. 3 seed Huntingtown (9-2). "They've got some good players."
But in a season that started with Easton being ranked 10th in one preseason poll, the Warriors showed they too had some good players.
"We had a tremendous year," said Griffith, whose team was one of only three Bayside Conference teams still playing last Friday along with defending Class 2A state champion Stephen Decatur and Cambridge-South Dorchester, the overall No. 1 seed in Class 1A whose undefeated season also ended in the rain and wind.
There have been other Easton teams that posted better records.
But over the past 40 years, no Warriors team had ever won two playoff games in the same season. Perhaps more impressive is no Easton team over that same time frame enjoyed a greater turnaround from one season to the next.
The Warriors lost starting quarterback Mikey O'Connor in Week 2 of the 2023 season and struggled to a 1-8 finish. O'Connor returned this season and helped Easton to an 8-4 record. The closest any previous Warrior team came to that seven-win improvement was in 1979, when Easton finished 9-1 after a 3-7 slate the previous year.
"We had a good year," said Griffith, who finished with his highest win total in his 10 years as Easton's head coach, and earned his 50th career win with the Warriors' 28-21 victory over Kent Island in the second round of the 2A East Regional playoffs. "The kids bought into the process in the offseason, which I think made a big difference, including Mikey. Mikey put on 15, 20 pounds and I think that was the difference in him being able to do what he did this year versus not being able to finish the (previous) year."
Though Easton's senior quarterback completed just 4 of his 14 attempts for 30 yards and an interception Friday, he rushed for 189 yards and a touchdown on a career-high 33 carries. O'Connor finished the season 127 for 242 through the air for 1,938 yards, 21 touchdowns and 15 interceptions. He also led the team in rushing, carrying 219 times for 1,436 yards and 19 touchdowns.
There were plenty of other parts to Easton's success this year.
A fleet of receivers that included Chase Raab, Diontaye Copper, Zach Barnhart and brothers Colin and Carter Mooney took turns making big catches and plays week after week. There was also the emergence of junior running back Dustin Blue, who became a brute force inside and out, totaling 652 yards and seven touchdowns.
Then there was an offensive line, that lost four starters from 2023 for various reasons. But together with sole returner Tymiere Thomas at right tackle, center TJ Truxon, guards Jack Chappell and freshman Brady Gilliece, and left tackle Xavier Stowers steadily developed and improved.
"Jack Chappell stepped up and started at right guard," Griffith said. "He gives you everything he has every play. TJ Truxon played center and did a good job for us this year. We had an outstanding freshman in Brady Gilliece at left guard, who I think is going to be one helluva player over the next couple years. And then we had sophomore left tackle in Xavier Stowers. And every so often we'd mix in Jaden Prestwood to give some guys some breaks. But those five pretty much played iron man football on the offensive line all year long."
Senior place-kicker Dominic Stanco also proved to a consistent weapon.
"He got better as the season went on and had a strong leg," Griffith said of Stanco. "It's a shame this is the only year he played football and he's a senior."
Not to be overshadowed was a defense that despite giving up its share of big plays, showed grit and delivered plenty of big stops and came up with timely takeaways. Jordan Horsey and Kyree Acree led the Warriors in tackles under the guidance of new defensive coordinator Al Waters. Thomas again proved an interior anchor up front, while Prestwood developed into a problem for opponents with his ability to play tackle, end and linebacker.
"Everything we tried to get out of them I think we got," Griffith said. "They gave it to us. They should be proud of their accomplishments for sure. And hopefully this is a part about setting a standard moving forward of what we're trying to do. But I think we got all the juice out of this squeeze, and maybe even a little bit of pulp."

title: Seahawks on record pace
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Seahawks on record pace

 November 27, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports

 Stephen Decatur High made history last year when it became the first Bayside Conference school to win a state football championship in 26 years.Not quite one year later, the Seahawks are making yet another historic bid. But don't expect head coach Jake Coleman to get overly excited just yet.
"I don't think being on the cusp of history means a whole lot," Coleman said. "It just means you ain't done it. It's kind of like when people say, 'You've got potential.'"
The top-seeded Seahawks (12-0) can put themselves in position to challenge for a second straight state title match Friday, when they host No. 4 seed Westlake (10-2) in a Class 2A state semifinal at 6:30 p.m. in Berlin.
A win would also give defending-champion Decatur at chance to challenge for a second consecutive title, something that hasn't been done since Coleman slipped on his helmet and fastened his chin strap for Cambridge-South Dorchester in 1995 and '96.
Coleman thought his team had the chance to contend for a second straight state title this season, despite the graduation of his son and starting quarterback Brycen Coleman, and fellow standouts Gavin Solito and Careen Bolden. Decatur's head coach also knew Brycen's successor behind center, junior Johnny Hobgood, needed support from this year's senior cast.
"Last year on the offensive side you had an extra special player obviously with Brycen," said Coleman, whose son now plays flex tight end at Vanderbilt. "And he had some guys around him that he was able to lift up and show them the way."
So before this season began, Coach Coleman told seniors and Division I commits Davin Chandler (Vanderbilt), Trybe Wise (Georgetown) and Ethan Bradshaw (Army), as well as his offensive line, it was their turn to provide support.
"I told them, 'Johnny's got really, really big shoes to fill,"' Jake Coleman said. "'So I don't want to hear that the ball was not perfect. I don't want to hear any excuses. We got to play like guys with experience and we got to start playing like Division I athletes, too.' And they really have. And they've given Johnny the pocket that's clean. He's thrown balls and they've made plays. And really it's been exactly what I knew was possible for this group."
Hobgood has been outstanding, completing 107 of 157 passes for 1,824 yards, 30 touchdowns and just two interceptions. He's also run for four touchdowns.
"Johnny Hobgood is playing as well offensively as any player in Bayside history," Coleman said. "And the thing you won't see within those stats is he's played probably 90 percent of the games this year only playing two quarters, because we've been running the clock on people."
Hobgood injured his leg during the Seahawks' 2A East Regional first-round victory over North Caroline. He sat out Decatur's 19-14 second-round win over Wicomico, but returned for last Friday's 37-0 state-quarterfinal rout of Walkersville, completing 8 of 13 for 93 yards and four touchdowns.
"Johnny throws the ball on time," Coleman said. "He's accurate. He can make plays with his legs when he needs to. But Johnny is that pro-style quarterback, where he throws on time and he's accurate, and he goes through his reads and his process."
Then there's that supporting cast.
Chandler has 29 receptions for 676 yards and eight touchdowns. Wise has snagged 28 passes for 512 yards and a team-high 10 TDs. Evan Copeland has 24 catches for 323 yards and seven touchdowns. And Zakhari Baker has totaled 26 grabs for 420 yards and seven touchdowns.
"Zakhari Baker, he starts the season off with a kickoff return for a touchdown and I don't think he's slowed down since," Coleman said. "He has just made explosive play after explosive play all season long. We have other good wide receivers, but Zahkari Baker has just been amazing this year."
Coleman said the same thing of running back Vernon DeShields, who's carried 97 times for 803 yards and 10 touchdowns.
Decatur also had a big hole to fill at inside linebacker with Solito's graduation. But that was the lone loss on a defense that returned its other 10 starters, and put together a string of five straight shutouts this year. Filling Solito's void have been linebackers Peyton Travers and Kyle Mumford.
That group prepares for its toughest test of the season in Westlake, which is led by senior running back Devin Cox (180 carries, 1,554 yards, 29 touchdowns) and junior quarterback William Drakeford Jr. (103 of 164, 1,169 yards, 14 touchdowns, 4 interceptions).
"Super fast," Coleman said of the Wolverines, who have shut out six of their last eight opponents. "They are probably the fastest defense that we have seen.
"Offensively, they're a power football team," Coleman added. "They got a really good running in (Cox), and he's tough to tackle. They've got an athletic dual threat quarterback. They've got weapons on the outside. It's exactly who you expect to see out a 10-2 semifinal team. They're definitely a team that has the ability to win it."
So does Decatur.
"This is right where I thought we'd be, is being contender," Coleman said. "Last year we were young. Now, we have experience. They're senior laden and they've been through the fire. Now, we just want to get ourselves back to Annapolis (site of the state title game)."

title: Decatur bids for second straight state title in rematch with Huntingtown
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Decatur bids for second straight state title in rematch with Huntingtown

 December 6, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports

 His team was undefeated and still wearing the tag of defending state champion.And though Stephen Decatur High trailed 14-0 at halftime in last Friday's Class 2A state semifinal, Seahawks head coach Jake Coleman said he felt no stress.
"I was pretty calm. Having to win a game when your son's a senior and it's the state championship, that was pressure," said Coleman, whose son Brycen quarterbacked Decatur to last year's 2A state crown.
"We came out very determined," Coleman said of last Friday's semifinal against Westlake. "I told them, 'Hey, we just got to get that first score.'"
But then the Wolverines widened their advantage to 20-0 with 3 minutes, 34 seconds left in the third quarter.
"I just told the guys, 'Keep fighting. Keep coaching,'" Coleman said. "Yeah, we were at the precipice of breaking, but we didn't. And we kept saying, 'Hey, get one score and then get one stop.' And as soon as we got the score, it was like, you could feel something changing on the field. Our guys were like, 'Oh, OK. We're still good.'"
The Seahawks proved to be real good, reeling off the game's final 27 points for a 27-20 overtime victory that launched them into Saturday's Class 2A state title game against Huntingtown (10-2) at 3:30 p.m. at Navy-Marine Corps Memorial Stadium in Annapolis.
A win Saturday would make Decatur (13-0) only the fourth football team in Bayside history to win back-to-back state titles, joining James M. Bennett (1982-83), Kent County (1989-90) and Cambridge-South Dorchester (1995-96).
"So now we have the challenge," Coleman said of the rematch with Huntingtown, which Decatur defeated 21-13 in last year's title game. "I told my seniors that are returning state champions, I was like, 'Hey. Are you satisfied? You got your ring. We got other guys that don't have a ring. I know they're going to be ready and they want it. And in practice this week, in the game, I don't know when, but you've got to answer that bell. Is this something you want?
"'You want to go back-to-back?'" Coleman continued. "'Because I can tell you this, Huntingtown has been thinking about you just like you were thinking about Milford Mill (which eliminated Decatur in the 2022 state semifinals, then lost to the Seahawks in last year's semis), and how you were waiting for the opportunity to go and beat them. Everything they've done has been for this moment. So they got the edge and now you've got to answer that question. Do you want it more than they want it? Do you want to go back-to- back?' We'll find out Saturday."
Of course, it wasn't looking like there would be a rematch with Westlake holding a 20-0 lead deep into last Friday's third quarter. That's when Coleman got into his defense.
"I told them, 'No excuses, man,'" Coleman said. "'This offense has been making it easy for us all year. It's our time to step up.' When we got the (first) score, we said, 'Hey, let's get 'em three-and-out. And if we get three-and-out, I promise you that offense is going to score.' And they did. We went three-and-out, and boom. We go right down field like we have done on many teams this season."
Decatur's comeback began when junior quarterback Johnny Hobgood connected with Zakhari Baker for a 38-yard touchdown pass with 34 seconds left in the third, and Blake Wallace booted the extra point, pulling the Seahawks within 20-7.
The defending champs pared their deficit to 20-14 with 6:15 left in the game on Nate Tapley's 2-yard touchdown run and Wallace's PAT.
"Once we got it to 20-14, I could just tell our guys were so determined," Coleman said. "I saw Johnny Hobgood transform. He goes from the first half really struggling, and then I saw him all of a sudden start to get that look. Everything just slowed down. Our offensive line starting handling them a little bit better."
Davin Chandler caught a 10-yard touchdown pass from Hobgood with 1:03 left, but Wallace missed the extra point, leaving the game knotted at 20-all and forcing overtime.
Westlake opted to go on defense first. Hobgood scored on an 8-yard run and Wallace converted the PAT to make it 27-20 before Decatur's defense stopped the Wolverines on their OT possession.
Now, comes Saturday's rematch.
"They're a premier program," Coleman said of the Huntingtown. "They're running the ball a little bit more than last year. Last year they were a little bit more balanced run to pass. This year a little bit heavier in the run in the games that we've seen. They certainly can pass unquestionably, and they are great on defense."
The Hurricanes' ground game is led by senior Landon Cawley (101 carries, 670 yards, 13 touchdowns) and juniors Gabriel Copeland (93-666-8) and Brody Whittington (53-542-5). Senior quarterback Dominic Hickman has completed 63 of 116 passes for 920 yards, six touchdowns and six interceptions.
Senior defensive end Evan Powell, a West Virginia University commit, is part of a defensive unit that will look to contain the Seahawks' run and passing game.
Hobgood has connected on 120 of his 190 attempts this season for 1,973 yards, 32 touchdowns and just two interceptions. His receiving fleet includes Chandler (36 receptions, 762 yards, 9 touchdowns), who Wednesday signed with Vanderbilt, and Trybe Wise (29-521-10), who signed with Georgetown. The Canes also have Baker (28-457-8) to contend with, and a running attack led by Vernon DeShields (106 carries, 855 yards, 10 touchdowns).
"You look across the board, all the teams that are playing in the state championship, all of them can run the ball," Coleman said. "All of them have good defenses. All of them have quarterbacks that most of the time are dual-threat kids. And they got playmakers. They are good in all three phases and they're well coached. And Huntingtown is no different.
"And I know that they are hungry," added Coleman of the Hurricanes, who are making their fourth state championship appearance. "(They) haven't been able to win one yet. It's going to be a great challenge."

title: Decatur rallies for second straight state title
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Decatur rallies for second straight state title

 December 10, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 1039

 Read News Document

 ANNAPOLIS — One minute. Three plays.That's all it took.
That's all Stephen Decatur High's football team needed Saturday to score the game-winning touchdown for a 13-12 victory over Huntingtown that earned the Seahawks a second straight Class 2A state championship, and completed a second consecutive 14-0 season at Navy-Marine Corps Memorial Stadium.
"To come back on a team like that is unbelievable," Seahawks head coach Jake Coleman said after beating the Hurricanes for a second straight year in the title game.
Especially considering after two strong game-opening drives — one ending with a touchdown for a 7-0 first-quarter lead, the second ending with a missed field goal — the Seahawks' high-octane offense was virtually silenced by Huntingtown.
"All the teams in the state championship games have great defenses year in and year out," Coleman said. "Because you can't get there without having a really tough defense. And Huntingtown's good. They made us struggle."
Those struggles came after Decatur took the opening kickoff and crafted a 12-play, 68-yard scoring march that ended with Nathan Tapley stretching across the goal line for a 2-yard touchdown run and Blake Wallace booming the extra point for a seven-point lead with 5:55 left in the first quarter.
The Seahawks were on the verge of widening that lead on their next possession, when a high snap from center on third-and-goal at the Huntingtown 1-yard line resulted in a 14-yard loss, setting up Wallace's 32-yard field goal attempt that sailed wide left. While those two plays, penalties, and a rare Johnny Hobgood interception hurt the Seahawks, the Hurricanes held the defending state champions to just 30 yards and two first downs on 20 plays over Decatur's next five possessions.
Huntingtown (10-3) trimmed its deficit, cobbling together an 18-play, 80-yard march that ended with Landon Cawley's 2-yard touchdown run with 7:05 left in the third quarter. But the Hurricanes couldn't pull even, as Decatur's Sully Auker delivered one of the season's biggest plays, blocking Max Hall's point-after attempt, keeping the Seahawks in front at 7-6.
Huntingtown then took the lead, when quarterback Dominic Hickman (13 carries, 108 yards) found room on the right side, and didn't stop until he had raced 57 yards for a touchdown and a 12-7 lead with 3:02 left in the game. Again Decatur came up big on the conversion attempt, stuffing Cawley (28 carries, 127 yards) one yard short on the two-point try.
Decatur's Davin Chandler returned the ensuing kickoff 22 yards, setting the Seahawks up at their own 39 with 2:58 left.
Eight days earlier, Decatur faced an even greater deficit when it trailed Westlake 20-0 with 3:34 left in the third quarter of the state semifinal before rallying for a 27-20 overtime victory.
Now, once again, Decatur's shot at history was in jeopardy.
Saturday, Decatur had less than 3 minutes to achieve what only three other Bayside Conference schools — James M. Bennett (1982-83), Kent County (1989-90) and Cambridge-South Dorchester (1995-96) — had done in winning back-to-back state titles. Perhaps more impressive, the Seahawks were less than 3 minutes away from becoming just the second Bayside program to win back-to-back state championships while going undefeated, joining John Usiltion's Bennett teams that went a combined 24-0 on the way to the '82 and '83 titles.
But this was different.
This a smaller window of time that was closing by the second.
And this was a defense that had proved much stingier than anything the Seahawks had faced before, holding Decatur to its lowest point total in two seasons — not counting the 1-0 season-opening forfeit over Queen Anne's in 2023.
But none of that seemed to matter to Decatur. There was no panic on the Seahawks' sideline from players or coaches. Instead, the offense calmly returned to the field led by the ever efficient Hobgood, who completed 17 of 21 passes for 233 yards in the game, and sounded more like a veteran signal-caller than a first-year starter at quarterback.
"Take what they give us," Hobgood said in the postgame press conference. "If it's short, take it."
He did just that, finding Vernon Deshields for a modest 5-yard pickup on first down that moved Decatur to their 44.
"If it's there deep, take that too," Hobgood said.
He did that, connecting with Trybe Wise for a pivotal 32-yard gain to the Hurricanes 24 on the next play.
"We had to be patient," Coleman said of the final drive. "We wanted to be patient with our game plan. They were a very good team and they were coached up very well. But we were trying to set guys up and that's what (offensive coordinator) Russell (Croteau) did on that last drive; went to some plays that we knew and had a probability of being some long gains."
The last of those high-probability calls came on the next play, when Hobgood looked left and tossed a 24-yard rainbow into Zakhari Baker's hands for a touchdown and a 13-12 Decatur lead with 1:58 left in the game.
"I had a feeling I was going to be open," said Baker, who got behind his defender to haul in the game-winning score. "I told Johnny, 'Trust me. I got you.' I just went up and got it."
Coleman wasn't surprised.
"When Johnny threw the ball I thought there's only one guy on the team that can go get that one," Coleman said of Baker.
Hobgood's two-point pass attempt fell incomplete.
Trent DePompa returned the ensuing kickoff 13 yards to the Hurricanes' 26. A 12-yard pass from Hickman to Trevor Robbins pushed Huntingtown to its 44. Auker sacked Hickman for a 4-yard loss. After two incompletions, Decatur was flagged for defensive holding on fourth down, setting up a fourth-and-four from the Seahawks' 35. But Hickman's final pass fell incomplete, sealing Decatur's victory.
"It was 100 percent about repeating," Coleman, who played on Cambridge-SD's back-to-back state title teams, said of his team's objective from the beginning of the season. "Make no mistake about it.
"My son told me, 'Hey Dad. You ain't won one without me,'" Coleman said of son Brycen, who quarterbacked the Seahawks to last year's title. "And I was like, 'OK.' And I whispered that into a couple of guys' ears. And I also told them at the beginning of the year, 'It's your time. You're the superstars now.' And they played like it. Two-time state champion. 28-0. What else can you say?"
